steps.message:
# RL training run diagnosis

Review the staged post-training experiment and determine whether it is healthy
or unhealthy. Treat the workspace as a historical snapshot: inspect its source,
effective configuration, launch scripts, data processing, reward logic, logs,
tracked metrics, and frozen evaluation evidence. Do not assume that an unusual
setting or implementation is causal without connecting it to observed behavior.

Use held-out evaluation evidence together with rollout, truncation, runtime,
optimization, and training signals. Training reward alone does not establish
held-out health. A truncated log is not by itself proof of a defect.

Do not launch a full training run, use the network, or modify the historical
snapshot. The dataset, held-out set, model, training-step budget, and evaluation
interval are fixed.

## Deliverable

Write one concise UTF-8 diagnosis to:

```text
$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/agent_answer.md
```

State the verdict, identify the concrete root cause or causes, and explain the
causal chain using specific workspace evidence. Distinguish root causes from
symptoms. Do not propose or implement a fix, and do not write other deliverable
files.
I'll start by surveying the workspace structure.

=== run.sh ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat, decoupled PPO with KPop (bidirectional binary-KL) token masking on GSM8K (AReaL, local scheduler).
# 3 epochs = 87 steps on one 8-GPU node: 4 SGLang rollout servers + 4 FSDP actor ranks
# (the allocation and every other default come from examples/math/gsm8k_icepop.yaml).
# The recorded run resolved the model and dataset by hub id from an offline cache
# (actor.path=Qwen/Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat, dataset path openai/gsm8k, see config.yaml);
# here they point at the local copies that environment/prepare.sh places in the workspace.
set -euo pipefail
W="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
cd "$W"
export PYTHONPATH="$W${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}"

SEED="${SEED:-2}"
RLROOT="${RLROOT:-$W/run}"
MODEL_PATH="${MODEL_PATH:-$W/models/Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat}"
DATA_PATH="${DATA_PATH:-$W/data/gsm8k}"
mkdir -p "$RLROOT/experiments" "$RLROOT/name_resolve" "$RLROOT/logs"

export HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 HF_DATASETS_OFFLINE=1 HF_HUB_DISABLE_PROGRESS_BARS=1
export TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false
export AREAL_ALLOW_DEFAULT_ADMIN_KEY=1
export PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
# Per-token logprob dumps (inference-engine / proximal / current), every 20th call.
export KT_DUMP_DIR="$RLROOT/ktdump/seeds_kpop_s${SEED}"
export KT_DUMP_EVERY=20
# Only read by disk-mode weight updates; this run syncs weights over NCCL (xccl).
export KT_WEIGHT_UPDATE_DIR="/dev/shm/${USER:-root}-wu-$$"

python examples/math/gsm8k_rl.py \
    --config examples/math/gsm8k_icepop.yaml \
    experiment_name=kt-seeds \
    trial_name=kpop-s${SEED} \
    seed=$SEED \
    scheduler.type=local \
    cluster.fileroot="$RLROOT/experiments" \
    cluster.name_resolve.nfs_record_root="$RLROOT/name_resolve" \
    actor.path="$MODEL_PATH" \
    train_dataset.path="$DATA_PATH" \
    valid_dataset.path="$DATA_PATH" \
    actor.optimizer.lr=3e-6 \
    actor.optimizer.weight_decay=0.01 \
    ++actor.eps_clip=0.2 \
    ++actor.eps_clip_higher=0.28 \
    actor.mb_spec.max_tokens_per_mb=4096 \
    ref.mb_spec.max_tokens_per_mb=4096 \
    ++train_dataset.setup_timeout=900 \
    ++valid_dataset.setup_timeout=900 \
    ++rollout.setup_timeout=900 \
    total_train_epochs=3 \
    actor.weight_update_mode=xccl \
    actor.request_timeout=3600 \
    rollout.request_timeout=3600 \
    vllm.disable_custom_all_reduce=false \
    actor.rejection_sampling.metric=binary_kl \
    actor.rejection_sampling.upper=2.0 \
    ~actor.rejection_sampling.lower

export KT_DUMP_EVERY=20
# Only read by disk-mode weight updates; this run syncs weights over NCCL (xccl).
export KT_WEIGHT_UPDATE_DIR="/dev/shm/${USER:-root}-wu-$$"

python examples/math/gsm8k_rl.py \
    --config examples/math/gsm8k_icepop.yaml \
    experiment_name=kt-seeds \
    trial_name=kpop-s${SEED} \
    seed=$SEED \
    scheduler.type=local \
    cluster.fileroot="$RLROOT/experiments" \
    cluster.name_resolve.nfs_record_root="$RLROOT/name_resolve" \
    actor.path="$MODEL_PATH" \
    train_dataset.path="$DATA_PATH" \
    valid_dataset.path="$DATA_PATH" \
    actor.optimizer.lr=3e-6 \

    ++actor.eps_clip=0.2 \

    actor.mb_spec.max_tokens_per_mb=4096 \

    ++train_dataset.setup_timeout=900 \

    vllm.disable_custom_all_reduce=false \

=== icepop yaml ===
experiment_name: gsm8k-icepop
trial_name: trial0

seed: 1
enable_offload: false
total_train_epochs: 10
tokenizer_path: ${actor.path}

cluster:
  n_nodes: 1
  n_gpus_per_node: 8
  fileroot: /tmp/areal/experiments
  name_resolve:
    type: nfs
    nfs_record_root: /tmp/areal/name_resolve


scheduler:
  type: null

rollout:
  backend: "sglang:d4p1t1"
  request_timeout: 10800   # disk weight reload of 30B over NFS can exceed the 3600s default
  experiment_name: ${experiment_name}
  trial_name: ${trial_name}
  max_concurrent_rollouts: 256
  queue_size: null
  consumer_batch_size: ${train_dataset.batch_size}
  max_head_offpolicyness: 2
  enable_rollout_tracing: false
  scheduling_spec: ${actor.scheduling_spec}
  fileroot: ${cluster.fileroot}
  tokenizer_path: ${tokenizer_path}
  dump_to_file: false
  agent:
    mode: inline
    export_style: individual
    turn_discount: 1.0

gconfig:
  n_samples: 4
  min_new_tokens: 0
  max_new_tokens: 1024
  max_tokens: 2048
  greedy: false
  temperature: 1.0

actor:
  backend: "fsdp:d4p1t1"
  request_timeout: 10800
  experiment_name: ${experiment_name}
  trial_name: ${trial_name}
  path: Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct
  init_from_scratch: false
  disable_dropout: true
  gradient_checkpointing: true
  dtype: bfloat16
  mb_spec:
    max_tokens_per_mb: 10240
    packing_algorithm: ffd
  optimizer:
    type: adam
    lr: 1.70e-5
    weight_decay: 0.017
    beta1: 0.9
    beta2: 0.999
    eps: 1e-8
    lr_scheduler_type: constant
    gradient_clipping: 1.0
    warmup_steps_proportion: 0.001
  eps_clip: 0.4
  temperature: ${gconfig.temperature}
  reward_scaling: 10.0
  reward_bias: -0.5
  kl_ctl: 0.0
  ppo_n_minibatches: 1
  use_decoupled_loss: true
  rejection_sampling:
    level: token
    action: mask
    metric: ratio
    lower: 0.5
    upper: 5.0
  reward_norm:
    mean_level: group
    std_level: group
    group_size: ${gconfig.n_samples}
  adv_norm:
    mean_level: batch
    std_level: batch
  weight_update_mode: disk   # xccl to vLLM hangs (FSDP all-gather waits forever); disk reload works
  max_new_tokens: ${gconfig.max_new_tokens}
  scheduling_spec:
    - task_type: worker
      port_count: 2
      gpu: 1
      mem: 32
      cmd: python3 -m areal.infra.rpc.rpc_server
      env_vars: {}

ref:
  backend: ${actor.backend}
  experiment_name: ${experiment_name}
  trial_name: ${trial_name}
  path: ${actor.path}
  init_from_scratch: false
  disable_dropout: true
  dtype: ${actor.dtype}
  mb_spec:
    max_tokens_per_mb: 10240
    packing_algorithm: ffd
  optimizer: null
  scheduling_strategy:
    type: colocation
    target: actor
  scheduling_spec: ${actor.scheduling_spec}

# SGLang
sglang:
  model_path: ${actor.path}
  random_seed: ${seed}
  skip_tokenizer_init: true
  dtype: ${actor.dtype}
  max_running_requests: null
  context_length: 32768
  mem_fraction_static: 0.8

vllm:
  model: ${actor.path}
  seed: ${seed}
  skip_tokenizer_init: false
  disable_custom_all_reduce: true
  dtype: ${actor.dtype}
  max_model_len: 32768
  gpu_memory_utilization: 0.8

# datasets
train_dataset:
  batch_size: 256
  shuffle: true
  pin_memory: true
  num_workers: 4
  path: openai/gsm8k
  type: rl
  max_length: 1024

valid_dataset:
  batch_size: 256
  pin_memory: true
  num_workers: 4
  path: openai/gsm8k
  type: rl

# Utilities
saver:
  experiment_name: ${experiment_name}
  trial_name: ${trial_name}
  fileroot: ${cluster.fileroot}
  freq_epochs: 1
  freq_steps: null
  freq_secs: null

recover:
  mode: disabled
  experiment_name: ${experiment_name}
  trial_name: ${trial_name}
  fileroot: ${cluster.fileroot}
  freq_epochs: 1
  freq_steps: null
  freq_secs: 3600

evaluator:
  experiment_name: ${experiment_name}
  trial_name: ${trial_name}
  fileroot: ${cluster.fileroot}
  freq_epochs: 1
  freq_steps: null
  freq_secs: null

stats_logger:

import sys

from areal import PPOTrainer
from areal.api.cli_args import GRPOConfig, load_expr_config
from areal.dataset import get_custom_dataset
from areal.utils.hf_utils import load_hf_tokenizer


def main(args):
    config, _ = load_expr_config(args, GRPOConfig)
    tokenizer = load_hf_tokenizer(config.tokenizer_path)

    train_dataset = get_custom_dataset(
        split="train",
        dataset_config=config.train_dataset,
        tokenizer=tokenizer,
    )
    valid_dataset = get_custom_dataset(
        split="test",
        dataset_config=config.valid_dataset,
        tokenizer=tokenizer,
    )

    workflow_kwargs = dict(
        temperature=config.gconfig.temperature,
        top_p=config.gconfig.top_p,
        max_tokens=config.gconfig.max_tokens,
        max_completion_tokens=config.gconfig.max_new_tokens,
    )
    eval_workflow_kwargs = workflow_kwargs.copy()
    eval_workflow_kwargs["temperature"] = 0.6

    with PPOTrainer(
        config,
        train_dataset=train_dataset,
        valid_dataset=valid_dataset,
    ) as trainer:
        trainer.train(
            workflow="areal.workflow.openai.math_agent.MathAgent",
            workflow_kwargs=workflow_kwargs,
            eval_workflow="areal.workflow.openai.math_agent.MathAgent",
            eval_workflow_kwargs=eval_workflow_kwargs,
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(sys.argv[1:])

The keys list lacks ppo_actor/task_reward/avg even though line 159 contains it, so the block parser drops pairs and I need to redo the extraction. My leading suspicion is train/eval mismatch: if weight updates never reach the rollout engine, rollouts stay on the base policy, keeping training reward near 0.70 while the actor trains against stale samples and degenerates, so eval on fresh weights gives 0.02. Against this, the eval engine shows collapse, so it did receive updated weights. I check logp_diff/avg rising 0.005 to 0.30, importance_weight/max growing 8.6 to 24, prox_logp_gt/max at -1.19e-07, no_eos_ratios/avg frozen at 0.00391, masked tokens growing 1.18k to 1.76k, rs_filtered_fraction about 8%. The KD-side numbers alone cannot decide this, so I read the decoupled loss, rejection sampling and binary_kl code, the checkpoint save and eval path, the KT parquet schema, the gsm8k train/test split, and the 368/344 rollout log errors. This gives the reward trajectory and the real cause.

The one number that decides whether the model truly degraded or the external eval is broken is the in-training validation accuracy on the GSM8K test split.
steps.reasoning_content:
The user is asking for a private read on the training run and then a single batch request for everything I need that doesn't depend on other results.

Let me work through what the metrics actually say. Training reward rises from 0.718 to 0.824 and then plateaus, while held-out gsm8k falls from 0.555 to 0.0205 - a collapse of roughly 27x. That gap is the central fact.

Entropy/avg drops from 0.183 to about 0.08, with a dip to 0.066 at step 40, and entropy/min sits near 1e-11. So the policy is collapsing toward near-determinism on some sequences. correct_seq_len/avg shrinks from 281 to 195, so answers are getting shorter.

The decoupled-loss signals are striking. prox_logp_gt max is always -1.1921e-07, i.e. prox_logp is never above old_logp - a systematic one-directional bias between the inference engine's logprobs and the training engine's recompute. logp_diff/avg grows from 0.005 to 0.30 nats. With entropy at 0.08, small logit differences translate into large logprob ratios, so the mismatch and the collapse reinforce each other. masked_token_ratio climbs from 0.30 to 0.44 under rejection sampling with binary_kl upper=2.0, and n_masked_tokens rises 1180 to 1760, so nearly half the tokens are being dropped by the end. behave_approx_kl/avg goes -0.006 to -0.10, kl_div_dual/avg 0.006 to 0.108, and grad_norm spikes to 202 at step 71.

no_eos_ratios/avg is frozen at 0.00391 = 1/256 across all 87 steps - exactly one sequence per batch without EOS, suspiciously constant while everything else moves.

The remaining puzzle is whether the model truly degraded or the external suite is broken. The in-training valid_dataset is also gsm8k split=test, evaluated every epoch, so its accuracy trajectory discriminates the two. The eval errors ("All output_tokens are EOS or PAD tokens") suggest degenerate outputs, but minerva only moves 0.0404 to 0.0368 while gsm8k falls from 0.555 to 0.0205 - inconsistent with uniform eval breakage.

What I need next: (a) the per-epoch in-training eval accuracy from main.log around timeperf/eval; (b) any stats jsonl/csv dumps under run/experiments; (c) a numeric comparison of old_logp vs prox_logp vs cur_logp across the three ktdump timestamps (steps 0, 680, 1340), including how often prox differs from old and mean absolute difference; (d) the rejection-sampling and decoupled-loss implementation to pin down binary_kl masking and mask_no_eos_with_zero semantics; (e) a count of eval episodes that errored versus succeeded in eval-rollout.log against the 1319 gsm8k samples, plus any successful completions; (f) a look at the gsm8k test parquet to confirm split correctness and answer format. None of these depend on each other's results, so I request them together.

import pyarrow.parquet as pq, glob, os, statistics
files=sorted(glob.glob('run/ktdump/seeds_kpop_s2/*.parquet'))
groups={}
for f in files:
    t=pq.read_table(f).to_pydict()
    key=os.path.basename(f).split('_')[1]  # timestamp
    groups.setdefault(key,[]).append((os.path.basename(f),t))
for ts,lst in sorted(groups.items()):
    old=[];prox=[];cur=[];ver=[]
    for name,t in lst:
        old+=t['old_logp']; prox+=t['prox_logp']; cur+=t['cur_logp']; ver+=t['version']
    n=len(old)
    import math
    d=[p-o for p,o in zip(prox,old)]
    dc=[c-p for c,p in zip(cur,prox)]
    print(f"== ts={ts} files={len(lst)} n={n} versions={sorted(set(ver))}")
    print(f"   mean(old)={statistics.mean(old):.4f} mean(prox)={statistics.mean(prox):.4f} mean(cur)={statistics.mean(cur):.4f}")
    print(f"   mean(prox-old)={statistics.mean(d):.5f} max={max(d):.5f} min={min(d):.5f} frac>0={sum(1 for x in d if x>0)/n:.4f}")
    print(f"   mean|prox-old|={statistics.mean(abs(x) for x in d):.5f}")
    print(f"   mean(cur-prox)={statistics.mean(dc):.5f} mean|cur-prox|={statistics.mean(abs(x) for x in dc):.5f}")
    # identical?
    print(f"   prox==cur exactly: {sum(1 for p,c in zip(prox,cur) if p==c)}/{n}")
EOF

    Args:
        proximal_logprobs: Proximal policy log-probabilities,

            f"proximal_logprobs shape {proximal_logprobs.shape} != "
            f"old_logprobs shape {old_logprobs.shape}"

            f"Expected 1D (packed) or 2D (padded) tensors, "
            f"got ndim={proximal_logprobs.ndim}"

def compute_binary_kl_divergence(
    log_p: torch.Tensor, log_q: torch.Tensor, eps: float = 1e-8
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """KL(P||Q) for Bernoulli distributions parameterized by log-probabilities.
    Treats each element as a Bernoulli: P = [p, 1-p], Q = [q, 1-q].
    KL(P||Q) = p*log(p/q) + (1-p)*log((1-p)/(1-q))
    """
    p = torch.clamp(torch.exp(log_p), eps, 1.0 - eps)
    q = torch.clamp(torch.exp(log_q), eps, 1.0 - eps)
    return p * torch.log(p / q) + (1 - p) * torch.log((1 - p) / (1 - q))


def ppo_actor_loss_fn(
    logprobs: torch.Tensor,
    proximal_logprobs: torch.Tensor,
    old_logprobs: torch.Tensor,
    advantages: torch.Tensor,
    eps_clip: float,
    loss_mask: torch.Tensor,
    eps_clip_higher: float | None = None,
    c_clip: float | None = None,
    rejection_sampling: RejectionSamplingConfig | None = None,
    importance_sampling_level: str = "token",
    cu_seqlens: torch.Tensor | None = None,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, dict]:
    """PPO actor loss function with optional rejection sampling.

    The ``rejection_sampling`` parameter replaces the removed
    ``behave_imp_weight_cap`` / ``behave_imp_weight_mode``.

    - ``action='mask'``: modifies loss_mask before loss computation (rejection)
    - ``action='clamp'``: clamps importance weight to bounds (truncation)

    When decoupled loss is disabled:
    1. if recompute logp, both old_logprobs and proximal_logprobs are recomputed logp;
    2. if no recomputation, both old_logp and proximal_logprobs are produced by the inference backend.

    When decoupled loss is enabled, proximal_logprobs is the recomputed logp,
    old_logprobs is produced by the inference engine.

    Note: ``importance_sampling_level`` controls PPO ratio (π_θ/π_proximal)
    aggregation (GSPO), which is orthogonal to ``rejection_sampling.level``
    that controls staleness filtering (π_proximal/π_behave) granularity.

    Args:
        logprobs: Current policy log-probabilities (π_θ).
        proximal_logprobs: Proximal policy log-probabilities (π_proximal).
        old_logprobs: Behavior policy log-probabilities from inference (π_behave).
        advantages: Per-token advantage estimates.
        eps_clip: PPO clipping factor for policy ratio.
        loss_mask: Mask for valid tokens (1 = valid).
        eps_clip_higher: Upper clipping factor (decoupled clipping). None = use eps_clip.
        c_clip: Dual clipping factor, must be > 1.0. None disables dual clipping.
        rejection_sampling: Rejection sampling configuration. None disables filtering.
        importance_sampling_level: Level at which to compute importance sampling ratios.
            - 'token': Per-token ratios (standard PPO)
            - 'sequence': Sequence-level geometric mean of per-token ratios (GSPO)
        cu_seqlens: Cumulative sequence lengths for packed sequences (1D tensors).
            Required when inputs are 1D and importance_sampling_level='sequence'.
            Shape: [batch_size + 1], where cu_seqlens[i] marks the start of sequence i.
            Not needed for 2D padded inputs (sequences identified by batch dimension).
    """
    # Save original count BEFORE rejection sampling may modify loss_mask.
    # This keeps the denominator consistent with loss_weight_fn in actor.py,
    # which always uses the original loss_mask from input_data. Without this,
    # mask mode would inflate per-token gradients by N_original / N_kept.
    loss_mask_count = loss_mask.count_nonzero() or 1
    # Pre-filter mask kept for ratio/clip statistics: rejection sampling below
    # narrows loss_mask for the loss, but stats stay on the original mask so
    # importance_weight/avg reads 1.0 under proximal reuse instead of
    # 1 - filtered_fraction. Gradients are unaffected: the final loss still
    # zeroes filtered tokens through the narrowed mask.
    stat_loss_mask = loss_mask

    # === Apply rejection sampling (replaces old compute_behave_imp_weight) ===
    if rejection_sampling is not None:
        rs_result = apply_rejection_sampling(
            proximal_logprobs=proximal_logprobs,
            old_logprobs=old_logprobs,
            loss_mask=loss_mask,
            cu_seqlens=cu_seqlens,
            config=rejection_sampling,
        )

        loss_mask = rs_result.loss_mask

        behave_imp_weight = rs_result.behave_imp_weight
        filtered_fraction = rs_result.filtered_fraction
    else:
        filtered_fraction = 0.0

    if importance_sampling_level == "sequence":
        # GSPO: Compute sequence-level geometric mean of probability ratios
        log_ratio = logprobs - proximal_logprobs
        ratio, advantages = _compute_sequence_level_ratio_and_advantages(
            log_ratio, advantages, loss_mask, cu_seqlens
        )
    elif importance_sampling_level == "token":
        # Standard PPO: per-token ratio
        ratio = torch.where(stat_loss_mask, torch.exp(logprobs - proximal_logprobs), 0)
    else:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Invalid importance_sampling_level: {importance_sampling_level}. "
            "Must be 'token' or 'sequence'."
        )

    clipped_ratio = torch.clamp(
        ratio,
        1.0 - eps_clip,
        1.0 + (eps_clip if eps_clip_higher is None else eps_clip_higher),
    )

    pg_loss1 = -advantages * ratio
    pg_loss2 = -advantages * clipped_ratio
    clip_mask = pg_loss1.detach() < pg_loss2.detach()
    pg_loss = torch.max(pg_loss1, pg_loss2)

        pg_loss = torch.min(pg_loss, pg_loss3)
    else:

    if rejection_sampling is not None:

        behave_mask = (behave_imp_weight > 0).logical_and(loss_mask.bool())
        behave_approx_kl = torch.where(behave_mask, behave_approx_kl, 0.0)
        pg_loss = pg_loss * behave_imp_weight

    logging_loss = pg_loss.detach()
    pg_loss = torch.where(loss_mask, pg_loss, 0).sum() / loss_mask_count

    dual_clip_mask.logical_and_(stat_loss_mask)
    # One host sync per microbatch: the count feeds three derived stats.
    n_stat_total = stat_loss_mask.numel()
    n_stat_valid = stat_loss_mask.count_nonzero().item()
    stat = dict(
        loss=logging_loss,
        importance_weight=ratio.detach(),
        approx_kl=(logprobs - proximal_logprobs).detach(),
        clip_mask=clip_mask,
        dual_clip_mask=dual_clip_mask,
        n_total_tokens=float(n_stat_total),
        n_valid_tokens=float(n_stat_valid),
        n_masked_tokens=float(n_stat_total - n_stat_valid),
        masked_token_ratio=1.0 - n_stat_valid / max(n_stat_total, 1),
    )

    if rejection_sampling is not None:

            behave_approx_kl=behave_approx_kl.detach(),
            behave_imp_weight=behave_imp_weight.detach(),
            behave_mask=behave_mask,
            filtered_fraction=filtered_fraction,
        )
    return pg_loss, stat

        loss_mask: Mask for valid tokens

        cu_seqlens: Cumulative sequence lengths for sequence-level IS

            "Must be 'token' or 'sequence'."

    gate_neg = torch.sigmoid(tau_neg * (ratio - 1.0))
    scale_pos = 4.0 / tau_pos
    scale_neg = 4.0 / tau_neg

    soft_gate = torch.where(is_positive, scaled_gate_pos, scaled_gate_neg)

    logging_loss = pg_loss.detach()
    pg_loss = torch.where(loss_mask, pg_loss, 0).sum() / loss_mask_count

    stat = dict(

    dual_clip_mask.logical_and_(stat_loss_mask)

    n_stat_total = stat_loss_mask.numel()
    n_stat_valid = stat_loss_mask.count_nonzero().item()

import sys

from areal.api.alloc_mode import ModelAllocation
from areal.api.cli_args import GRPOConfig, SGLangConfig, load_expr_config, vLLMConfig
from areal.dataset import get_custom_dataset
from areal.engine import RemoteSGLangEngine, RemotevLLMEngine
from areal.infra import LocalScheduler, RayScheduler, SlurmScheduler
from areal.utils import logging, seeding
from areal.utils.dataloader import create_dataloader
from areal.utils.hf_utils import load_hf_tokenizer
from areal.utils.printing import tabulate_stats

logger = logging.getLogger("GSM8KEval")


def main(args):
    config, _ = load_expr_config(args, GRPOConfig)
    logging.setup_file_logging(f"{config.cluster.fileroot}/eval.log")

    tokenizer = load_hf_tokenizer(config.tokenizer_path)
    seeding.set_random_seed(config.seed, key="eval")

    rollout_alloc = ModelAllocation.from_str(config.rollout.backend, name="rollout")

    # Initialize scheduler
    cfg = config.scheduler
    if cfg.type == "local":
        scheduler = LocalScheduler(exp_config=config)
    elif cfg.type == "ray":
        scheduler = RayScheduler(exp_config=config)
    elif cfg.type == "slurm":
        scheduler = SlurmScheduler(exp_config=config)
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown scheduler type: {cfg.type}")

    # Load evaluation dataset
    valid_dataset = get_custom_dataset(
        split="test", dataset_config=config.valid_dataset, tokenizer=tokenizer
    )
    valid_dataloader = create_dataloader(
        valid_dataset,
        rank=0,
        world_size=1,
        dataset_config=config.valid_dataset,
    )

    # Initialize RolloutController
    config.rollout.max_head_offpolicyness = int(1e12)

    if rollout_alloc.backend == "sglang":
        engine_cls = RemoteSGLangEngine
        server_args = SGLangConfig.build_args(
            sglang_config=config.sglang,
            tp_size=rollout_alloc.parallel.tp_size,
            base_gpu_id=0,
        )
    elif rollout_alloc.backend == "vllm":
        engine_cls = RemotevLLMEngine
        server_args = vLLMConfig.build_args(
            vllm_config=config.vllm,
            tp_size=rollout_alloc.parallel.tp_size,
            pp_size=rollout_alloc.parallel.pp_size,
        )
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid backend: {rollout_alloc.backend}")

    eval_rollout = engine_cls.as_controller(config.rollout, scheduler)

    try:
        eval_rollout.initialize(
            role="eval-rollout",
            server_args=server_args,
        )

        # Create evaluation workflow
        workflow = "areal.workflow.rlvr.RLVRWorkflow"
        workflow_kwargs = dict(
            reward_fn="areal.reward.gsm8k.gsm8k_reward_fn",
            gconfig=config.gconfig,
            tokenizer=config.tokenizer_path,
            enable_thinking=False,
        )

        # Submit all evaluation tasks
        cnt = 0
        for data in valid_dataloader:
            for item in data:
                eval_rollout.submit(
                    item,
                    workflow=workflow,
                    workflow_kwargs=workflow_kwargs,
                    group_size=config.gconfig.n_samples,
                )
                cnt += 1

        eval_rollout.wait(cnt, timeout=None)
        eval_stats = eval_rollout.export_stats()

        # Print and log results
        logger.info(f"Evaluation Results: {tabulate_stats(eval_stats)}")
    finally:
        eval_rollout.destroy()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(sys.argv[1:])

Firing those in one batch.
steps.reasoning_content:
The user is asking whether the final checkpoint's collapse to roughly 2% on every benchmark traces back to training, to the weight-sync path, or to how the checkpoint is saved and served, and they want the answer grounded in the numbers already collected rather than in the unusual settings alone.

Let me lay out what the logs actually establish. The run completes 87 steps. Training reward rises from 0.718 to 0.824 while held-out accuracy on the same GSM8K test split falls to 0.0197. That is not domain-specific overfitting, because math500 drops from 0.212 to 0.026, svamp from 0.59 to 0.023, and olympiad from 0.049 to 0.0148. Minerva sits at 0.0404 before and 0.0368 after, essentially unchanged, so the checkpoint still emits something parseable occasionally; it is not producing pure EOS everywhere.

The in-training eval gives nothing to lean on: timeperf/eval stays near 2e-5 seconds at every step, so no held-out evaluation actually ran during training. The only held-out evidence is the external suite TSV, run on the saved checkpoint.

The inference-versus-training logprob gap is the strongest internal signal. mean(prox-old) starts at -0.004 and reaches -0.16 nats per token by step 84, with mean|prox-old| growing from 0.027 to 0.199, max behave_imp_weight reaching 24, and masked_token_ratio climbing from 30% to 44% under binary_kl with upper=2.0. Entropy falls from 0.18 to 0.066 and correct_seq_len shrinks from 281 to 195 tokens, which is policy sharpening, and sharpening is exactly when a confident token under prox and a mismatched q under behave makes binary KL exceed 2.0.

The ktdump line where prox equals cur exactly is consistent, not a bug: prox is recomputed before the update, cur logp comes from the training forward pass at the same pre-update weights, and there is one microbatch, so identical values are expected.

The grad norm spike to 202 at step 71 and the eps_clip_higher=0.28 asymmetry are ordinary stress, not corruption. So the arithmetic points to training-side drift amplified by the growing prox/old mismatch, not to a corrupt export: a corrupt checkpoint would push minerva to 0 as well. That mismatch, whether from numerics divergence or partial weight sync during sharpening, is what I would carry forward.

steps.message:
Facts on the table so far, and what's still missing before I call it.

**Established:** 87/87 steps completed; training reward rose 0.72 → 0.82 and entropy fell 0.18 → 0.08; answer length shrank; the prox-vs-inference logprob gap grew from 0.03 to 0.20 nats/token; the final checkpoint's eval rollouts emit immediate EOS; the frozen suite shows gsm8k 0.555 → 0.0205 with every other benchmark collapsing too.

**Still needed, independent items:**
1. The save/checkpoint timeline, so I know which weights the suite and the failing eval actually scored.
2. Whether the in-training evaluator ever produced a number (its timer reads 2e-5 seconds, which looks like a no-op).
3. Provenance of the `final_checkpoint_suite.tsv` rows: harness, model path, prompt format.
4. Whether the generation path is hitting length limits vs EOS, and what `no_eos_ratios` measures.
5. The trainer's decoupled-loss plumbing: where `old`, `prox`, and `cur` logprobs come from.
6. Any checkpoint artifacts on disk.

Requesting all six now.
steps.reasoning_content:
The user is asking for a diagnosis that sets up the training run: 87 steps, 3 epochs, lr 3e-6, 8 GPUs, Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat. The training reward climbs from 0.718 to 0.824, rollout/reward tracks it, while entropy falls from 0.183 to ~0.08 with a mid-training spike. The held-out suite shows the collapse: gsm8k 0.555 → 0.0205, math500 0.212 → 0.026, svamp 0.59 → 0.023, olympiad 0.049 → 0.0148, minerva 0.0404 → 0.0368. That 0.0205 gsm8k figure is 27/1319, essentially zero correct answers on numeric GSM8K. The training split is 7473, test is 1319, and the same local gsm8k path feeds both train and valid via the config default. The in-run evaluator shows timeperf/eval of 2e-5, so no actual eval ran in the train loop; eval-rollout workers fork at 01:52 and three tasks fail at 02:55 with "All output_tokens are EOS or PAD tokens" and "This trajectory will be rejected." The eval-rollout log runs 221 lines and is truncated at shutdown, so the in-training eval never produces a scored number.

The real evidence is the final-checkpoint suite: 0.555 → 0.0205 on the same gsm8k test where the training reward on the same distribution reaches 0.85. The EOS observation directly links the two: the final policy emits immediate EOS, so every benchmark scores near zero. The uniform collapse across math500, svamp, olympiad, minerva, and gsm8k fits a degenerate model rather than forgetting, because overfitting to 7473 GSM8K examples explains a drop on math500 but not five benchmarks dropping at once.

The secondary symptoms: seq_len 293→200, max 1200→419; logp_diff 0.005→0.34 nats/token; ktdump mean|prox-old| 0.027→0.199 with mean(prox-old) −0.16 and max logp diff −21.6; prox_logp_gt/max ≈ −1.19e-7 showing a systematic gap rather than symmetric noise; masked_token_ratio 0.30→0.44; behave_imp_weight/max 8.6→24; grad norm 202 at step 71; kl_ctl=0.0 leaves no reference anchor. The mismatch means SGLang and FSDP see very different logprobs: old_logp/avg −0.18→−0.21 against ktdump mean(old) −0.088 and mean(prox) −0.25 at step 84, a 0.16 nat/token gap that inflates per-token importance weights. Generation caps at max_completion_tokens=1024 because MathAgent pops max_tokens. Weight sync runs under weight_update_mode=xccl at timeperf/update_weights ~3s, so weights reach the engine and training reward climbing confirms that. The saved checkpoint at the epoch boundary versus the trained actor is the remaining suspect for EOS-only output, since the training rollouts still produce 200-token answers.

steps.message: Working through the evidence, my open questions are: (1) did the in-run evaluator report any valid-set accuracy at the epoch boundaries, (2) which weights the frozen suite scored, (3) where the saved checkpoint was written and whether the export path is suspicious, (4) how prox/old logprobs are resolved, and (5) what the full 129-key metric table shows at the last steps. Firing those now.
steps.reasoning_content:
The user is asking whether the RL training run was healthy, and if not, what the root cause is, laying out the causal chain. I start with what the evidence shows. The eval suite TSV is the only artifact in the workspace, and it shows the final checkpoint collapsing on all benchmarks: gsm8k 0.555 -> 0.0205, svamp 0.59 -> 0.0233, math500 0.212 -> 0.026, olympiad 0.049 -> 0.0148, minerva 0.0404 -> 0.0368. The minerva number moves least because it sits near floor already, which is consistent with complete output degeneracy rather than a policy that learned something specific. Meanwhile the training rollouts show reward 0.82 and sequence lengths around 200-300 tokens, so training-time generation is not broken. That gap is the thing to explain: training reward rises while the exported checkpoint scores near floor on every benchmark.

I consider the candidate causes. A broken or partially synced checkpoint (FSDP -> HF conversion bug) would produce exactly this collapse while training looks fine, since the live xccl weight updates drive the 0.82 reward but the saved shards are what the suite loads. A second candidate is the systematic logprob gap: mean(prox - old) is about -0.16 nats/token, so inference-side and training-side logprobs disagree persistently. A third is the entropy collapse from 0.18 to 0.08 combined with masked_token_ratio climbing to 0.44, showing the binary-KL masking strips a large fraction of tokens as the run progresses.

The evidence I still need to separate these is the in-training validation accuracy at steps 29 and 58 (timeperf/eval shows a 131.3 s eval, so eval does run at epoch boundaries), whether any of the 129 stats keys carry an accuracy metric, provenance of the suite harness since nothing on disk besides the TSV exists, and the save/checkpoint conversion path plus _resolve_proximal_logp. If validation accuracy at steps 29 and 58 is healthy but the final checkpoint reads 0.02, the collapse is at export, not in the policy. The training-side signals (entropy 0.08, 44% masked tokens, -0.16 nats/token logprob offset) then become symptoms of an off-policy drift that the masking is absorbing, not the direct cause of the benchmark floor.

            logger.info(f"  Proximal policy (π_prox): {desc}")

            logger.info("  log_p_theta (π_θ): TRAINING FORWARD PASS (current policy)")

            if config.rejection_sampling is not None:

        reward_score = data["rewards"]
        reward_score = (reward_score + self.reward_bias) * self.reward_scaling
        reward_score = torch.clip(

        # Use actual trajectory group sizes when available so group-level
        # normalization handles failed/filtered rollout samples without slicing

        group_sizes = meta.traj_group_sizes if meta is not None else None

        loss_mask = torch.roll(loss_mask, shifts=-1, dims=-1)
        # Apply the mask to log probabilities.

            # Overwrite logprobs produced by the inference engine
            prox_logp_value = data["prox_logp"]

            old_logp = data["logprobs"] = prox_logp_value

        seqlens = attn_mask.sum(-1).long()

        kl_rewards = rewards.clone()
        # KL rewards at the next token after eos is zero.

        indices = torch.clip(seqlens - 2, min=0)
        if self.mask_no_eos_with_zero:
            rewards[batch_indices, indices] += torch.where(
                seq_no_eos_mask, 0, reward_score
            )
        else:
            rewards[batch_indices, indices] += reward_score

        # Compute GAE.
        if "values" not in data:
            values = torch.zeros_like(rewards)
        else:
            values = data["values"]
        advantages_reversed = [
            torch.zeros(bs, dtype=torch.float32, device=values.device)
        ]
        lastgaelam = 0
        nextvalues = values[:, max_seqlen - 1] * seq_no_eos_mask
        for t in reversed(range(max_seqlen - 1)):
            delta = rewards[:, t] + self.discount * nextvalues - values[:, t]
            newgaelam = delta + self.discount * self.gae_lambda * lastgaelam

            # Skip tokens that do not contribute to the loss
            mask = loss_mask[:, t]
            nextvalues = nextvalues * (1 - mask) + values[:, t] * mask
            lastgaelam = lastgaelam * (1 - mask) + newgaelam * mask
            advantages_reversed.append(lastgaelam)

        advantages = torch.stack(advantages_reversed[::-1], dim=1)
        data["returns"] = advantages + values

        # Optionally perform advantage normalization.
        if self.adv_norm is not None:
            # Use the same actual trajectory group sizes as reward normalization;
            # ignored when adv_norm is batch-level.
            advantages = self.adv_norm(advantages, loss_mask, group_sizes=group_sizes)

        # Store data in the dict.
        data["advantages"] = advantages
        data["kl_rewards"] = kl_rewards
        data["tot_rewards"] = rewards
        data["loss_mask"] = loss_mask
        # because we have rolled old_logp by -1
        data["logprobs"] = old_logp

        return data

        # Use actual trajectory group sizes when available so group-level
        # normalization handles failed/filtered rollout samples without slicing
        # across prompts. Direct calls without batched metadata keep the legacy
        # fixed-group-size behavior.
        group_sizes = meta.traj_group_sizes if meta is not None else None
        if self.reward_norm:
            reward_score = self.reward_norm(reward_score, group_sizes=group_sizes)

        loss_mask = data["loss_mask"].float()
        loss_mask = torch.roll(loss_mask, shifts=-1, dims=-1)
        # Apply the mask to log probabilities.
        if not self.config.use_decoupled_loss and self.config.recompute_logprob:
            # Overwrite logprobs produced by the inference engine
            prox_logp_value = data["prox_logp"]
            if prox_logp_value is None:
                raise ValueError(
                    "prox_logp is None but recompute_logprob=True. "
                    "This indicates compute_logp() was skipped incorrectly."
                )
            old_logp = data["logprobs"] = prox_logp_value
        else:
            old_logp = torch.roll(data["logprobs"], shifts=-1, dims=-1)
            if not self.config.use_decoupled_loss:
                # prox logp not available, use inferenced logp
                data["prox_logp"] = old_logp
        ref_logp = data.get("ref_logp")
        if ref_logp is None:
            ref_logp = torch.zeros_like(old_logp)
        ref_logp *= loss_mask
        old_logp *= loss_mask

        # Compute KL-regularized rewards.
        attn_mask = data["attention_mask"]
        seqlens = attn_mask.sum(-1).long()
        seq_no_eos_mask = seqlens == attn_mask.shape[1]
        rewards = -self.kl_ctl * self.kl_estimator(old_logp, ref_logp)
        kl_rewards = rewards.clone()
        # KL rewards at the next token after eos is zero.
        rewards[batch_indices, seqlens - 1] = 0
        indices = torch.clip(seqlens - 2, min=0)
        if self.mask_no_eos_with_zero:
            rewards[batch_indices, indices] += torch.where(
                seq_no_eos_mask, 0, reward_score
            )
        else:
            rewards[batch_indices, indices] += reward_score

        # Compute GAE.
        if "values" not in data:
            values = torch.zeros_like(rewards)
        else:
            values = data["values"]
        advantages_reversed = [
            torch.zeros(bs, dtype=torch.float32, device=values.device)
        ]
        lastgaelam = 0
        nextvalues = values[:, max_seqlen - 1] * seq_no_eos_mask
        for t in reversed(range(max_seqlen - 1)):
            delta = rewards[:, t] + self.discount * nextvalues - values[:, t]
            newgaelam = delta + self.discount * self.gae_lambda * lastgaelam

            # Skip tokens that do not contribute to the loss
            mask = loss_mask[:, t]
            nextvalues = nextvalues * (1 - mask) + values[:, t] * mask
            lastgaelam = lastgaelam * (1 - mask) + newgaelam * mask
            advantages_reversed.append(lastgaelam)

        advantages = torch.stack(advantages_reversed[::-1], dim=1)
        data["returns"] = advantages + values

        # Optionally perform advantage normalization.
        if self.adv_norm is not None:
            # Use the same actual trajectory group sizes as reward normalization;
            # ignored when adv_norm is batch-level.
            advantages = self.adv_norm(advantages, loss_mask, group_sizes=group_sizes)

        # Store data in the dict.
        data["advantages"] = advantages
        data["kl_rewards"] = kl_rewards
        data["tot_rewards"] = rewards
        data["loss_mask"] = loss_mask
        # because we have rolled old_logp by -1
        data["logprobs"] = old_logp

        return data

steps.reasoning_content: The user is asking me to work out why the final checkpoint scored 0.0205 in the frozen suite when the in-training evaluation reports about 0.60, and to decide whether the collapse comes from optimization or from the saved artifact. I start from the in-training validation numbers: eval-rollout/reward is 0.6073 at step 29, 0.6128 at step 58, and 0.6021 at step 87, while the external suite gives gsm8k 0.0205 for the final checkpoint against 0.5550 for suite_base, which is the untouched Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat. minerva moves only from 0.0404 to 0.0368 and olympiad from 0.0490 to 0.0148, so every benchmark sits at or below the floor rather than degrading along a competence gradient. A trained policy that still answers 60% of validation prompts correctly cannot plausibly produce a uniform 2% on the same test set, so the discrepancy has to live in the artifact or the eval configuration, not in the optimization dynamics. The near-constant validation reward across steps 29, 58, and 87 (0.6073, 0.6128, 0.6021) is itself worth flagging: it tracks the base model's 0.555-0.60 range almost exactly, which is consistent with either a genuinely stable held-out score or with the eval engine never seeing updated weights through set_version. The 3 "All output_tokens are EOS or PAD tokens" failures inside the step-87 eval log concern me less as a cause, since 3 rejections out of 1319 samples with n_samples=4 cannot move a 0.60 down to 0.02; immediate EOS emission for a handful of prompts is normal tail behavior. The training-side telemetry points the same direction: seq_len falls from 293 to 200 and entropy from 0.18 to 0.08, which is length compression, not the annihilation required to produce 0.02. On the recompute side, ktdump shows mean(prox-old) drifting from -0.004 at step 0 to -0.16 by step 84 with mean|prox-old| at 0.199, and cur equals prox exactly for every token because both come from a single forward pass before the optimizer step; prox_logp_gt/max pinned at -1.1921e-07 confirms the gap is one-signed. That is the fingerprint of a systematic engine-versus-trainer forward-pass difference of roughly 0.03 nats per token at step 0 that amplifies as the policy sharpens, not evidence of weight corruption. So the load-bearing question is provenance: which weights did suite_kpop_s2 actually load, and does the save path write the actor in a loadable HF layout given the 60-expert Qwen2Moe architecture under weight_update_mode xccl, with saver freq_epochs=1 and 130-144s save times at steps 29, 58, and 87. Both the frozen-suite provenance and the save-path layout are still unchecked.

steps.message: I need to settle four things before writing: whether the in-run evaluator ever saw updated weights, what the pathological KL/importance-weight spikes imply, how the checkpoint is exported, and whether the spikes line up with gradient explosions.
steps.reasoning_content: The user is asking me to work through the diagnosis myself, so let me set up what the numbers actually say. The audit has 87/87 steps. Training reward rises from 0.68 to 0.85, but the in-training eval on the GSM8K test set sits at 0.607, 0.613, 0.602 at steps 29, 58, 87, essentially flat around 0.60. The frozen suite on the final checkpoint gives gsm8k 0.0205, gsm8k_em 0.0197, math500 0.026, svamp 0.0233, minerva 0.0368, olympiad 0.0148, while the baseline gives 0.555, 0.536, 0.212, 0.59, 0.0404, 0.049. That gap between 0.60 in-training and 0.02 on the frozen suite is the crux. I check the floor effects: minerva moves 0.0404 to 0.0368, barely at floor, so it cannot distinguish a degraded model from a broken one. The 3 "All output_tokens are EOS or PAD tokens" errors at 02:55 are 3 out of 5276 rollouts, small. Entropy falls 0.18 to 0.08, seq_len/avg falls 360 to ~200, correct_seq_len/avg 281 to 195, so the policy sharpens and shortens, which fits partial degeneration alongside flat held-out accuracy. The prox-versus-behave logprob gap grows: mean(prox-old) from -0.004 to -0.16, mean|prox-old| 0.027 to 0.199, behave_imp_weight max 43 to 163 to 731, masked_token_ratio 30% to 44%, and prox_logp_gt/max ≈ -1.19e-7, meaning training-engine logprobs sit systematically below inference-engine logprobs. Two hypotheses fit the 0.60-versus-0.02 split: either the live model is fine at ~0.60 and the saved checkpoint is corrupt, or the in-training eval never received updated weights and always measured the base model. I cannot yet separate them. The decisive checks are whether eval-rollout actually received weight updates over xccl, and whether the HF export of the MoE checkpoint preserved its experts.

Working list of what's still missing:

1. Whether `eval_rollout` is even connected to the weight-update channel, or only `rollout` is; if it isn't, in-run eval was measuring a stale policy.
2. The full per-step series of `eval-rollout/reward` (does it exist at steps other than 29/58/87?).
3. The FSDP→HF save path: how weights are cast and saved for a 60-expert Qwen2MoE, and what `set_version`/save ordering does.
4. The evaluator's own semantics (temperature 0.6, n_samples 4, `drop_incomplete_group=False`) and whether it can score a degenerate policy as ~0.60 while an external harness gets 0.02.
5. Where `final_checkpoint_suite.tsv` comes from — any harness, manifest, or prepare script outside the workspace.
6. The rollout stop-reason/length distribution and whether EOS-only outputs occur only twice or systematically.

steps.reasoning_content: The user is asking me to review what remains to investigate. The in-run evaluator on the full 1319 GSM8K test items reports eval-rollout/reward of 0.6073 at step 29, 0.6128 at step 58, and 0.6021 at step 87, while the frozen external suite reports 0.0205. This is flat around the base level of 0.555, so the held-out reward neither rises nor collapses during training. The training reward itself moves from 0.72 to 0.82, sequence length drops from 280 to 200, and entropy falls from 0.18 to 0.08, so the policy does change. The suite's near-floor scores (math500 0.026, svamp 0.023, olympiad 0.0148) fit a model emitting EOS immediately rather than one overfit to GSM8K; overfitting would not take SVAMP from 0.59 to 0.023 while in-training GSM8K stays at 0.60. The "All output_tokens are EOS or PAD tokens" errors at 02:55 point the same way. My working hypothesis is that the step-87 export is corrupt or degenerate, not the SGLang-served weights. I check whether eval_rollout is connected via connect_engine alongside rollout, since if it is not, the flat 0.60 is stale base-model accuracy and the real collapse is in the trained checkpoint. Prox_logp_gt/max at −1.19e-7 confirms the training forward pass never exceeds the old logprob, matching the masked_token_ratio rise from 30% to 44% and behave_approx_kl avg from −0.006 to −0.10. With no checkpoints on disk (run/experiments holds 3.8M) I cannot inspect the saved directory directly, so the reads I need are rl_trainer.py lines 380-480, the FSDP save and compute-cast paths, evaluator.py for the temperature 0.6 setting, and any suite manifest under the parent directories.

# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

from collections.abc import Callable

from areal.api import FinetuneSpec
from areal.api.cli_args import EvaluatorConfig
from areal.utils import timeutil


class Evaluator:
    def __init__(self, config: EvaluatorConfig, ft_spec: FinetuneSpec):
        self.config = config
        self.ft_sepc = ft_spec
        self.freq_ctl = timeutil.EpochStepTimeFreqCtl(
            freq_epoch=config.freq_epochs,
            freq_step=config.freq_steps,
            freq_sec=config.freq_secs,
            initial_epoch_value=config.eval_before_train,
        )

    def state_dict(self):
        return self.freq_ctl.state_dict()

    def load_state_dict(self, state_dict):
        self.freq_ctl.load_state_dict(state_dict)

    def evaluate(
        self,
        evaluate_fn: Callable,
        epoch: int,
        step: int,
        global_step: int,
    ):
        if not self.freq_ctl.check(
            epochs=int(step == self.ft_sepc.steps_per_epoch - 1), steps=1
        ):
            return
        evaluate_fn()

steps.message: I have the trajectory and the code paths. Before writing, I need to resolve three open questions: whether the eval engine is on the weight-update path, whether a suite harness or prepare script exists in the snapshot, and what the repo's own KPop documentation says the expected behavior is.
steps.reasoning_content:
The user is asking me to identify why the final checkpoint from the Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat GSM8K run scores near-zero on the held-out suite despite the in-run eval looking flat, and to separate root cause from symptoms.

I start with the run facts: 7473 train samples at batch 256 give 29 steps/epoch, 3 epochs is 87 steps, and all 87 completed. lr is 3e-6, kl_ctl=0, decoupled PPO, rejection_sampling with binary_kl upper=2.0, action=mask, level=token. Training task_reward/avg goes 0.718 → 0.824, and correct_n_seqs at the first logged step is 735/1024 = 0.717. The held-out suite gives suite_base gsm8k 0.5550, math500 0.2120, svamp 0.59, minerva 0.0404, olympiad 0.0490, while suite_kpop_s2 gives gsm8k 0.0205. The other final numbers I place alongside it: math500 0.026, svamp 0.0233, olympiad 0.0148, minerva 0.0368. Base scores in the same harness are sane, so the harness itself works.

The in-run eval-rollout/reward at steps 29, 58, 87 is 0.607, 0.613, 0.602 on the GSM8K test split, which sits near the base 0.555. If the final weights really produced gsm8k 0.02, the in-run eval could not read 0.60. So the in-run eval is not measuring the final trained policy: eval_rollout is never connected to weight updates, since connect_engine targets rollout only, so it keeps scoring the initial weights and stays flat. That makes 0.60 uninformative about the final weights, not evidence of health.

Now the training-side signals. Entropy/avg falls 0.183 → 0.082 and correct_seq_len/avg shortens 281 → 195. prox_logp_gt max is -1.192e-07 at every step, meaning the training-side logprobs sit systematically below the inference-engine logprobs; the ktdump means are -0.088 for old and -0.25 for prox at step 84, and mean absolute diff grows 0.027 → 0.199. masked_token_ratio rises 0.30 → 0.44, so 44 percent of tokens leave the loss, while behave_imp_weight max reaches 731 at step 87. importance_weight/avg stays exactly 1 with ppo_n_minibatches=1, so clipping never activates and approx_kl is 0. That leaves a high-variance, systematically biased gradient estimator under kl_ctl=0 with no anchor to the base policy, which fits the entropy collapse and the shortening outputs. The "All output_tokens are EOS or PAD tokens" errors at 02:55 in the final eval, only 3 of them, are consistent with a policy that sometimes emits only EOS but are too few to prove anything alone.

So the collapse is real degradation of the policy under unchecked drift, the training reward rise is on-policy and not corroborating, the flat in-run eval is a symptom of the weight-update wiring, and the external suite numbers are the trustworthy evidence.

**Private list of what's still open:** (1) whether the in-run eval at steps 29/58/87 measured the trained weights or a stale/base model, since that decides whether the 0.60 vs 0.02 conflict is an eval artifact or a broken export; (2) the save path — `_save_training_state`, `Saver`, and async checkpoint mode — since a config-plus-tokenizer-only export with missing shards would produce exactly the near-chance suite scores; (3) whether eval-rollout talks to the same SGLang servers as rollout; (4) the on-disk format the export should produce for a Qwen2MoE checkpoint; (5) whether any save step errored or timed out; (6) what the `Submitted batch job` at the end of the run log is; (7) rollout acceptance/rejection and the end-of-run sequence.

steps.reasoning_content:
The user is asking me to work through what is still unresolved in this RL training investigation and then request the independent items I need in one response.

The facts I have: training reward rises 0.72 to 0.82 while entropy falls 0.18 to 0.08. In-training eval on GSM8K test (1319 samples) at steps 29/58/87 gives 0.607, 0.613, 0.602, flat near base. The external suite shows base gsm8k 0.555 falling to 0.0205 on kpop_s2, with math500 0.212 to 0.026, svamp 0.59 to 0.023, olympiad 0.049 to 0.0148, minerva 0.0404 to 0.0368. Training-side stats: seq_len/avg falls from ~290 to ~200, no_eos_ratios ~0.004 constant, masked_token_ratio rises 0.30 to 0.44. prox_logp_gt/max is -1.19e-07 always, ktdump mean(prox-old) = -0.16, mean|prox-old| = 0.199, old_logp ~ -0.088, prox ~ -0.25, and cur_logp equals prox_logp exactly. The final eval logs "All output_tokens are EOS or PAD tokens" 3 times. Saves take 143.9, 130.5, 130.0s.

The core contradiction I keep hitting: in-engine eval at step 87 scores 0.602 on gsm8k test, but the exported final checkpoint scores 0.0205 on the same benchmark through the external suite. The base model through the same suite scores 0.555, so the harness works for base. That gap means either the export is broken or the in-engine eval does not measure the updated weights. The in-engine eval reuses the same colocated rollout workers and servers, so it should see updated weights; but the eval reward barely moves across steps, which is also consistent with a static model. I need to decide between these.

I also need to know whether the collapse is real: uniform near-zero across every benchmark, including minerva which sits at floor, fits a model that emits EOS immediately or a corrupt/incorrectly-loaded checkpoint rather than ordinary overfitting. The 0.0205 is not zero, so something runs and produces garbage-ish output.

Independent items I request in one response:
1. The exported checkpoint directory listing and config.json/tokenizer files for the final save, to check whether export wrote a coherent MoE state dict and intact tokenizer/chat template.
2. Whether the external suite evaluated the HF export or the recover/fp32 checkpoint, and the exact load path.
3. The suite invocation details (prompt template, temperature, max tokens, stop strings) for base and kpop_s2 runs.
4. A dump comparing a few expert weight tensors between the in-engine model at step 87 and the exported checkpoint.
5. Whether eval-rollout actually received the weight broadcast at each step (version counter and broadcast logs).

A model whose weights were genuinely destroyed would not have shown 0.602 at step 87, so the disagreement has to come from what differs between the two paths: the HF export in `_save_full_model_to_hf`, which calls `get_model_state_dict(self.model, options=StateDictOptions(full_state_dict=True, cpu_offload=True))` and then `save_pretrained`. If the gathered keys carry a prefix mismatch against Qwen2MoeForCausalLM, `save_pretrained` writes them without validating, reload leaves the model randomly initialized, and every benchmark collapses toward chance at once. The uniform collapse across benchmarks never trained on, svamp from 0.59 to 0.0233 and math500 from 0.212 to 0.026, fits that far better than forgetting does under mild overfitting. The 3 occurrences of "All output_tokens are EOS or PAD tokens" out of 1319 fit a broken model emitting EOS first, even though their count is small.

The ktdump supports a secondary, separate story. At step 84, mean(prox-old) = -0.16, min -21.6, max +3.07, frac>0 at 0.33-0.47, and behave_imp_weight/max reaches 731.7 at step 87. Between step 0 and step 84, mean(old) rises from -0.186 to -0.088 while mean(prox) falls from -0.189 to -0.250. Under the decoupled loss, `prox` sets the PPO ratio reference and `old` sets the rejection-sampling weight, so a systematic 0.16-nat bias between the two engines inflates exp(prox-old) with heavy tails, though the binary_kl mask catches the extreme cases, which is consistent with masked_token_ratio growing 0.30→0.44. That is imperfect off-policy noise, not the cause of the collapse, since the same servers produced 0.602.

What I still need is the saved state dict key list versus the HF model's expected keys, the full save-time log around steps 29/58/87 (143.9s, 130.5s, 130.0s), the suite's prompt template and tokenizer config, and confirmation of whether the suite scored the step-87 save. Those four facts settle export corruption versus a real collapse.

steps.message:
Before I write anything, here's my remaining list: (1) whether the xccl weight-sync path handles `qwen2_moe` expert parameters, since the MoE-specific checks I saw only mention qwen3-moe/deepseek; (2) the exact `get_model_state_dict` import and full-tensor export path; (3) how `prox_logp` is recomputed and aligned versus `old_logp`; (4) the counterfactual question the numbers force — in-loop eval says 0.60 on the same 1319 items the frozen suite scores at 0.02.

Only (1)–(3) are independent, so I'll pull those now.
steps.reasoning_content:
The user is asking why the kpop_s2 checkpoint collapses from a base of 0.555 on gsm8k to 0.0205, despite the in-training eval reporting roughly 0.60. I work through the conflict directly.

The facts sit in tension. Training reward climbs 0.72 to 0.82, entropy falls 0.18 to 0.08, seq_len shrinks 293 to 200. The in-training eval at steps 29, 58, 87 reads 0.607, 0.613, 0.602, essentially flat at the 0.555 base. The frozen suite gives gsm8k 0.0205, math500 0.026, svamp 0.0233, olympiad 0.0148, minerva 0.0368. The same harness scores the base model correctly at 0.555, 0.212, 0.59, 0.049, so the harness itself works.

The ktdump pins the training-side mismatch. At step 0, mean(prox-old) is -0.0039 with mean|prox-old| 0.027 and frac>0 = 0.47. At step 38 it is -0.152 with mean|.| 0.187. At step 84 it is -0.161 with mean|.| 0.199, old_logp mean -0.088 against prox -0.250. cur equals prox exactly, 6332 of 6332, because both come from the same forward pass at the same weights. The metric prox_logp_gt/max holds at -1.1921e-07 every step: no token anywhere has prox above old. That is a structural one-sided offset, not noise. The gap grows as entropy falls, and 0.16 nats over 200 tokens is about 32 nats per sequence, so behave_imp_weight/max reaches 731, kl_div_dual/max 724, masked_token_ratio rises 30% to 44%, and rs_filtered_fraction ends at 43%. Since importance_weight/avg stays at 1.0 and approx_kl at 0, the clipped_tokens stay 0 and the update reduces to a plain advantage-weighted step on unmasked tokens.

The discriminator is minerva: 0.0404 to 0.0368, essentially unchanged. A corrupt or random checkpoint would score 0 on minerva too. So the checkpoint still generates parseable math. Meanwhile gsm8k drops 27x and svamp 25x while minerva holds, which fits a model that has drifted into a narrow output style the external answer extraction no longer parses, not a dead model. The flat 0.60 eval is consistent with the live policy still being intact while the exported format and sharpened distribution diverge from what the suite expects.

    def _update_weights_from_distributed(self, meta: WeightUpdateMeta):
        """Broadcast parameters with single-pending-bucket pipelining."""

        # Reset weight weight meta with local info
        meta.nccl_master_address = self.weight_update_master_addr
        meta.nccl_master_port = self.weight_update_master_port
        meta.nccl_group_name = (
            self.weight_update_group_names[0]
            if self.weight_update_group_names
            else "update_weight_group"
        )

        main_rank = dist.get_rank() == 0
        if main_rank:
            self.rollout_engine.pause_generation()

        dist.barrier(group=self.cpu_group)

        weight_chunked_mem_size = meta.weight_chunked_mem_mb * 1024 * 1024
        broadcast_stream = None

        if (
            main_rank
            and current_platform.device_type == "cuda"
            and torch.cuda.is_available()
        ):
            broadcast_stream = torch.cuda.Stream()

        buffer_size = 0
        named_tensors: list[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]] = []
        pending_bucket: _PendingWeightUpdateBucket | None = None

        if self.config.use_lora:
            # For LoRA, only iterate over trainable LoRA parameters
            param_iterator = (
                (name, param)
                for name, param in self._get_model_name_parameters(meta)
                if param.requires_grad
            )
        else:
            # For full model, iterate over all parameters
            param_iterator = self._get_model_name_parameters(meta)

        try:
            for name, param in param_iterator:
                # Ranks other than 0 only help to get the full tensor
                # (DTensor.full_tensor() is a collective; all ranks must
                # call _get_full_tensor). Only rank 0 broadcasts to the
                # rollout engine, so casting is main-rank-only by design.
                tensor = self._get_full_tensor(param)
                if not main_rank:
                    continue
                # Cast fp32 master storage to compute dtype before broadcast.
                # Rollout engines (SGLang/vLLM) expect compute dtype (bf16).
                tensor = self._cast_to_compute_dtype(tensor)

                tensor_size = tensor.numel() * tensor.element_size()
                bucket_overflow = (
                    buffer_size > 0
                    and tensor_size + buffer_size > weight_chunked_mem_size
                )
                if bucket_overflow:
                    # Only middle buckets need drain+align before the next all-gather.
                    if pending_bucket is not None:
                        self._wait_pending_weight_update_bucket(pending_bucket)
                        pending_bucket = None

                    pending_bucket = self._update_bucket_weights_from_distributed_async(
                        meta,
                        named_tensors,
                        stream=broadcast_stream,
                    )

                    named_tensors = []
                    buffer_size = 0

                buffer_size += tensor_size
                named_tensors.append((name, tensor))

            if pending_bucket:
                self._wait_pending_weight_update_bucket(pending_bucket)
                pending_bucket = None

            # Process remaining parameters
            if buffer_size > 0:
                self._update_bucket_weights_from_distributed(meta, named_tensors)
        finally:
            if main_rank and pending_bucket is not None:
                self._wait_pending_weight_update_bucket(pending_bucket)
                pending_bucket = None

def _resolve_proximal_logp(
    prox_logp_gt: torch.Tensor | None,
    prox_logp_method: str,
    old_logp: torch.Tensor,
    logprobs: torch.Tensor,
    versions: torch.Tensor | None,
    current_version: int | None,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """
    Resolve the proximal policy log-probabilities based on the method.

    This function determines the final proximal log-probabilities to use for PPO training,
    either from ground truth (forward pass) or approximation methods.

    Args:
        prox_logp_gt: Ground truth proximal logp (from forward pass), or None if skipped.
        prox_logp_method: Method to use (recompute, loglinear, metrics).
        old_logp: Behavior policy log-probabilities.
        logprobs: Current policy log-probabilities (should be detached).
        versions: Per-token policy versions, or None.
        current_version: Current training version, or None.

    Returns:
        Resolved proximal log-probabilities tensor.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If configuration is invalid (e.g., missing required data).
        RuntimeError: If computation fails (None result, NaN, Inf).
    """
    prox_logp_is_none = prox_logp_gt is None

    # Validate configuration when prox_logp is None
    if prox_logp_is_none:
        if not ProxLogpMethod(prox_logp_method).skips_forward_pass():
            raise ValueError(
                f"prox_logp is None but prox_logp_method='{prox_logp_method}'. "
                "This indicates compute_logp() was skipped incorrectly."
            )
        if versions is None:
            raise ValueError(
                f"prox_logp is None with prox_logp_method='{prox_logp_method}' "
                "but versions not available. "
                "Cannot proceed without either ground truth or approximation."
            )

    # Determine prox_logp based on method
    prox_logp = prox_logp_gt  # Default to ground truth (could be None)

    if prox_logp_method == PROX_LOGP_METHOD_LOGLINEAR:
        # Use loglinear approximation (must compute if prox_logp is None)
        if prox_logp_is_none and versions is not None and current_version is not None:
            approximations = compute_prox_logp_approximations(
                old_logp=old_logp,
                logprobs=logprobs,
                versions=versions,
                current_version=current_version,
                method=PROX_APPROX_METHOD_LOGLINEAR,
            )
            prox_logp = approximations[PROX_APPROX_METHOD_LOGLINEAR]
    elif prox_logp_method == PROX_LOGP_METHOD_METRICS:
        # Metrics mode: use recomputed prox_logp for training,
        # but will also compute approximation metrics later
        pass  # Use prox_logp_gt as-is (should be recomputed)
    # else: PROX_LOGP_METHOD_RECOMPUTE - use prox_logp_gt as-is

    # Safety check: ensure we have prox_logp
    if prox_logp is None:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"prox_logp is None after handling prox_logp_method='{prox_logp_method}'. "
            "This indicates configuration or computation error."
        )

    # Verify the value is valid
    if torch.isnan(prox_logp).any() or torch.isinf(prox_logp).any():
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"prox_logp contains NaN or Inf with prox_logp_method='{prox_logp_method}'. "
            "This indicates computation failed."
        )

    return prox_logp

The user is asking me to diagnose this staged post-training run and decide whether it is healthy, then name the concrete root cause. I work through the evidence.

Training reward climbs 0.72 → 0.82 and entropy falls 0.183 → 0.082, so the live policy is sharpening. The frozen suite numbers tell a different story: final checkpoint gsm8k 0.0205, gsm8k_em 0.0197, math500 0.026, svamp 0.0233, minerva 0.0368, olympiad 0.0148, against base 0.555, 0.212, 0.59, 0.0404, 0.049. Uniform near-zero collapse across every benchmark, including svamp 0.59 → 0.023, is degenerate output, not simple forgetting. The base numbers are sane, so the harness itself works and the checkpoint artifact is the problem.

The in-loop eval complicates this: same 1319 GSM8K test items give ~0.60-0.61 at steps 29, 58, 87 while the frozen suite gives 0.0205 on that same test set. Two explanations remain: a broken HF export (MoE weights dropped or misattributed) while live weights were fine, or the live eval scoring stale weights so 0.60 is essentially base performance. The xccl updates clearly reach the servers, since rollout reward rose 0.68 → 0.85, so stale weights are unlikely. That leaves the export path: `get_model_state_dict(..., full_state_dict=True)` then `save_pretrained(path, state_dict=...)` on a Qwen2MoE model loaded in float32 (the Flash Attention dtype warning confirms float32 load), with compile disabled so no `_orig_mod` prefix. Structural key matching looks right, so the failure is subtler than a prefix mismatch, but the contradiction itself is the finding.

Separately, the optimization signals are wrong. `prox_logp_gt` is ≤ 0 for every token, max -1.19e-07 (float32 rounding) but avg -0.20 and min -30. ktdump shows mean(old) -0.1855 vs mean(prox) -0.1894 at step 0, then -0.0837 vs -0.2358 by step 38, with frac>0 falling 0.47 → 0.333. The trainer's recomputed logprobs sit systematically below the engine's, and the gap grows to ~0.15 nats/token.

That bias drives rejection sampling: masked_token_ratio 0.30 → 0.44, behave_filtered_ratio 0.43, unclipped_behave_tokens 66780 of n_valid_tokens 1.159e5, behave_imp_weight/max 731. Nearly half the tokens are discarded. With prox_logp_method recompute and ppo_n_minibatches 1, importance_weight/avg stays exactly 1.0, approx_kl 0.0, clipped_tokens 0, so the ratio is identically 1 and clipping does nothing; the gradient is plain REINFORCE on surviving tokens.

The systematic prox < old gap is a train/inference mismatch, amplified because entropy 0.183 → 0.082 makes peaked distributions turn tiny logit differences into large logprob differences. Unhealthy run. Root causes: a broken or mis-exported final checkpoint, and a growing trainer/engine logprob mismatch that masks ~44% of tokens and leaves the update driven by a degenerate ratio-1 objective.

The user is asking which unknowns remain for the diagnosis, and all independent ones belong in a single request.

The training side is coherent: 87/87 steps, no crashes, task_reward 0.72→0.82, rollout reward 0.85, entropy 0.18→0.08, correct_seq_len 281→195. The in-loop eval on GSM8K test stays flat: 0.607 at step 29, 0.613 at step 58, 0.602 at step 87, against a base of 0.555. The frozen suite tells the opposite story: gsm8k 0.555→0.0205, math500 0.212→0.026, svamp 0.59→0.0233, olympiad 0.049→0.0148, minerva 0.0404→0.0368. Every benchmark collapses to near floor, which is what a bad artifact looks like, not what a policy that still answers 0.60 through SGLang looks like. The 3 "all output tokens are EOS/PAD" errors at 02:55, over roughly 1319 samples, are too few to explain the suite.

The trainer/inference mismatch is the second thread. prox_logp_gt/avg is negative at every step, max -1.19e-7, mean gap -0.004→-0.16 nats/token as entropy falls. ktdump gen tokens at step 84 show mean(prox-old) = -0.11 with frac>0 = 0.335, so two thirds of tokens have prox < old. KPop therefore masks more and more: masked_token_ratio 0.303→0.443, behave_filtered_ratio 0.078→0.43. Gradients come only from tokens where the two engines agree. The step-84 ktdump prompt tokens (version=-1) show mean(prox) = -12.6 against mean(old) = -0.23, which points at position alignment or packing in the recomputed forward, or at loss_mask leakage at the roll boundary. no_eos_ratios/avg is pinned at 0.00391 = 1/256 for all 87 steps, which reads like a stale or fixed count rather than a measurement.

What I still need to know: which checkpoint the suite_kpop_s2 rows loaded, and whether the same checkpoint, run through the in-loop MathAgent workflow, reproduces 0.60 or 0.02; whether the suite_base rows used the untouched HF model; whether the eval-rollout controller shares weight updates with the rollout servers or holds its own copy; whether the saved HF weights match the live FSDP weights by checksum or a spot logprob comparison; and how the prompt-token rows enter the loss mask despite the roll.

**Still missing (my list):** (1) whether the xccl weight broadcast enumerates and sends every parameter, especially the 60 MoE experts, and whether the bucketed pipelining can drop or reorder chunks; (2) where exactly the ktdump sits relative to rejection sampling, since the dump implies ~2% of tokens exceed the binary-KL bound while the logged filtered fraction is 43%; (3) how `eval-rollout`'s stats are aggregated (per-eval vs cumulative), because the three in-loop eval values sit flat at ~0.60 while the frozen suite scores the same final weights at ~0.02; (4) whether eval and rollout actually share SGLang server addresses; (5) the exact save/gather path for a 60-expert FSDP2 checkpoint; (6) dataset provenance.
steps.reasoning_content:
The user is asking me to work through the run's numbers myself and state what I actually conclude about the training signals versus the held-out collapse. Let me set up the quantities. Training reward rises 0.72 → 0.82 across 87 steps and 3 epochs. In-loop eval on the GSM8K test set gives 0.607, 0.613, 0.602 at steps 29/58/87 — flat, and only slightly above the base model's 0.555. The frozen final-suite gives gsm8k 0.0205, em 0.0197, math500 0.026, svamp 0.0233, minerva 0.0368, olympiad 0.0148. Both in-loop eval and the frozen suite score the same 1319-item GSM8K test set, so 0.602 and 0.0205 cannot both describe the same weights on the same data.

I check the drift signals. Entropy falls 0.183 → ~0.08; seq_len/avg falls 293 → 200; correct_seq_len/avg falls 281 → 195; masked_token_ratio rises 0.30 → 0.44. The KL dumps show gen-token mean(prox−old) drifting from -0.004 (step 0) to -0.14 (step 38) to -0.11 (step 84), with mean|diff| 0.027 → 0.187 → 0.199 and frac(prox>old) = 0.335 at step 84. Prompt tokens (version=-1) at ts=1786697568 show mean(old) = -0.23 versus mean(prox) = -12.6 with frac>0 = 0.000 on 44 tokens. That is a systematic train/inference mismatch on the same token sequence, and it grows as the policy sharpens. Behave_imp_weight/max reaches 731 and min 4e-11; prox_logp_gt/avg sits near -0.20 to -0.25 from the start. Mean(prox−old) drift from -0.004 to -0.16 means the loss weights average ~e^-0.16 ≈ 0.85, a constant scaling, but the tail at 731 dominates.

Approx_kl/avg is 0.0000 and importance_weight is 1.0 exactly, with clipped_tokens 0, so the PPO ratio is identically 1 and the update is advantage-weighted REINFORCE times behave_imp_weight. The 44% masking removes tokens where the mismatch is largest, so the surviving gradient is biased. The 3 "All output_tokens are EOS or PAD tokens" errors at 02:55 fall inside the final eval window but are only 3 of 5276 rollouts, so they don't explain a collapse to 0.02.

The contradiction stands: the live weights score ~0.60 in-loop, so if the saved checkpoint scores 0.0205, the artifact evaluated differs from the weights that were trained. The growth of the prox/old mismatch and the entropy collapse to 0.08 are real defects in the update, but they cannot turn a 0.60 policy into a 0.02 policy on the same test set. The decisive open item is the checkpoint export path and what the suite actually loaded, not the training reward curve.
