# Verdict: unhealthy

The run completed its budget (87/87 steps, 3 epochs), but the artifact it produced is
catastrophically degraded on held-out data. Training reward rose while held-out
capability collapsed to the floor of every benchmark in the frozen suite. The run's own
metrics could not see this, because the in-loop evaluator is built from the same prompt
and workflow as training.

## Held-out evidence (frozen suite, `run/eval/final_checkpoint_suite.tsv`)

| benchmark | base | kpop_s2 | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| gsm8k | 0.5550 | 0.0205 | -0.535 |
| gsm8k_em | 0.5360 | 0.0197 | -0.516 |
| math500 | 0.2120 | 0.0260 | -0.186 |
| svamp | 0.5900 | 0.0233 | -0.567 |
| minerva | 0.0404 | 0.0368 | -0.004 |
| olympiad | 0.0490 | 0.0148 | -0.034 |

Every benchmark lands at or below its near-chance floor, including SVAMP (0.59 -> 0.023),
which a merely overfit model cannot fall below. This is a degenerate checkpoint, not
mild forgetting.

## What the run looked like internally

- `ppo_actor/task_reward/avg` rose 0.718 (step 1) -> 0.824 (step 87), peaking 0.875;
  `rollout/reward` 0.680 -> 0.852.
- The in-loop epoch evaluations, on the 1319 GSM8K test items
  (`eval-rollout/reward`), were 0.6073 (step 29), 0.6128 (step 58), 0.6021 (step 87):
  flat at base level for all three epochs.
- Entropy fell 0.183 -> 0.082 nats/token (per-token `entropy/min` down to ~4e-12).
- Correct-answer length shrank 281 -> 195 tokens (max 625 -> 419); `seq_len/avg`
  293 -> 202; step time fell 32.5 s -> 18.7 s for this reason, not from a runtime fault.
- At the final eval, three trajectories were rejected with
  `All output_tokens are EOS or PAD tokens` (`eval-rollout.log` 02:55), i.e. the policy
  had begun emitting empty/EOS-only generations.

Train reward gain and flat epoch-eval accuracy together mean the gain was memorization:
7473 fixed prompts at batch 256 for three epochs (29 steps/epoch) is three exposures per
prompt, and the same-prompt held-out score never moved. The evaluator reuses the training
workflow (`examples/math/gsm8k_rl.py` passes `MathAgent` and the same `gconfig` to
`eval_workflow`), so 0.60 there measures only "still works on the exact training prompt".

## Root cause 1: the update signal was a cross-engine logprob bias, not policy improvement

Under `use_decoupled_loss=true` with `prox_logp_method=recompute`, the proximal policy is
recomputed in the FSDP trainer while `old_logp` is the inference engine's value. The two
engines disagree, and the disagreement grows monotonically:

- `logp_diff/avg` 0.0055 -> 0.306; `logp_abs_diff/avg` 0.029 -> 0.338 nats/token.
- `old_logp/avg` (inference) rises -0.181 -> -0.067 while `prox_logp_gt/avg` (trainer)
  stays ~-0.20: the serving engine becomes progressively more confident than the trainer
  on the same tokens.
- The per-token dumps (`run/ktdump/seeds_kpop_s2`) make this explicit: mean |prox-old|
  0.027 (step 0) -> 0.199 (step 84), with the fraction where prox > old falling 0.471 ->
  0.335 and `binary_kl > 2` tokens rising 0.02% -> 1.8%.

KPop then converts that bias into data loss: `rs_filtered_fraction` (the binary-KL mask)
rose 0.078 -> 0.434 and `behave_filtered_ratio/avg` 0.078 -> 0.43, so by the end 43% of
generated tokens were discarded because the two engines disagreed, not because the policy
was stale (`sample_staleness_proximal_avg` is 1 throughout, `v_proximal = v_theta - 1`).

## Root cause 2: PPO clipping is structurally inert, so nothing bounds the drift

The dumps show `cur_logp` and `prox_logp` are bit-identical (6332/6332 and 10397/10397
tokens), so the ratio pi_theta/pi_prox is exactly 1: `importance_weight/avg` and `/max`
are 1.000, `approx_kl/avg` is 0.000, and `clipped_tokens` is 0 for all 87 steps. The
entire gradient is therefore `-advantage * exp(prox-old)` on the surviving tokens, with
`kl_ctl=0.0` (no reference anchor). `behave_imp_weight/max` reaches 731.7 at step 87,
so a handful of tokens dominate each update; `grad_norm` spikes to 202 at step 71 (11.9
and 15.7 at steps 47/43). This is the path by which a low-entropy, short-output,
partly-EOS-only policy was reached while training reward kept rising.

## Symptoms (not causes)

- Rising train reward with flat held-out accuracy: memorization of a 3-epoch fixed set.
- Entropy halving, answer-length shrinkage, EOS-only generations: consequences of the
  unanchored, sparsely-masked update, and the direct precursor of the suite floor.
- Single-step gradient spikes: clipped at 1.0, so secondary.
- `masked_token_ratio` rising 0.30 -> 0.44: this is the prompt share of the batch growing
  as answers shortened (`n_valid_tokens` here is the pre-mask count), not extra masking.

## Ruled out as causes

- Truncation: `no_eos_ratios/avg` is essentially constant at 4/1024 = 0.0039 and
  `mask_no_eos_with_zero=false`; sequences hitting the length cap are not the driver.
- Runtime/log integrity: all 87 steps logged, saves at 130-144 s per epoch and xccl
  weight updates at 2.5-5.4 s; the log tail is a normal teardown followed by a new batch
  submission, not a crash. Step-time improvement tracks the shorter answers.
- Data: `data/gsm8k` is stock GSM8K (7473 train / 1319 test, every test answer carries
  `####`), and the reward (`math_verify.parse/verify`) is the same one the suite uses.

## Unresolved last hop

The snapshot contains no checkpoint files and no suite harness, so it cannot be settled
here whether the 0.02 floor is the exported artifact failing to reproduce the live
weights or the policy being unusable outside the exact training prompt. Either way the
chain is the same: the objective drifted the policy into a degenerate regime, and the
in-loop evaluator shared the training prompt and therefore reported a flat 0.60 while
the independent suite measured the collapse.
EOF

def bkl(lp,lq,eps=1e-8):
    p=min(max(math.exp(lp),eps),1-eps); q=min(max(math.exp(lq),eps),1-eps)
    return p*math.log(p/q)+(1-p)*math.log((1-p)/(1-q))

    else:
        high.append((math.exp(lr),k,math.exp(p),lr))
print("gen tokens",len(gen),"surviving",len(surv),"masked",len(high))
w=sorted(s[0] for s in surv)

big=[s for s in surv if s[0]>10]
print("surviving weight>10:",len(big))
for s in sorted(big,reverse=True)[:8]:

# relation: for tiny p, is binaryKL small despite big log ratio?
tiny=[s for s in surv if s[2]<1e-5 and s[0]>3]
print("surviving tokens with p<1e-5 and w>3:",len(tiny), "example:", tiny[:2])

**Private list of remaining unknowns:**

1. Whether `eval-rollout/reward` is per-eval or cumulative — decides whether the flat 0.60 at steps 29/58/87 is three clean held-out reads.
2. Whether `prox_logp_gt/max = -1.19e-07` is a numeric clamp artifact of the logging, not a real ceiling.
3. Whether the trainer's recomputed `prox` and the served `old` diverge because of one-step staleness alone or because the FSDP weights and SGLang weights are drifting apart — the key fork between "policy degenerated" and "served model diverged from trained model".
4. Whether SGLang's parameter-name matching would silently skip unknown names (partial weight updates).
5. Whether an HF export of this Qwen2MoE via the installed transformers keeps per-expert key names (export symmetry).
6. Whether any checkpoint/suite artifact exists anywhere on disk.
7. What `compute_logp` does (temperature, masking, versions) so the prox-vs-old gap is interpretable.

Items 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 are mutually independent. Requesting all in one batch.

def _log_proximal_approximation_stats(
    prox_logp_method: str,
    prox_logp_gt: torch.Tensor | None,
    old_logp: torch.Tensor,
    logprobs: torch.Tensor,
    versions: torch.Tensor | None,
    current_version: int | None,
    compute_logp_mask: torch.Tensor,
) -> None:
    """
    Log proximal policy approximation metrics based on the method.

    Args:
        prox_logp_method: The proximal logp method being used.
        prox_logp_gt: Ground truth proximal logp, or None if skipped.
        old_logp: Behavior policy log-probabilities.
        logprobs: Current policy log-probabilities (detached).
        versions: Per-token policy versions, or None.
        current_version: Current training version, or None.
        compute_logp_mask: Mask for valid tokens.
    """
    with stats_tracker.scope("compute_logp"):
        stats_tracker.denominator(n_valid_tokens=compute_logp_mask.bool())

        # Log ground truth when available
        if prox_logp_gt is not None:
            stats_tracker.stat(
                prox_logp_gt=prox_logp_gt.float(),
                denominator="n_valid_tokens",
            )

        # Skip if versions not available
        if versions is None or current_version is None:
            return

        if prox_logp_method == PROX_LOGP_METHOD_LOGLINEAR:
            # Loglinear mode: log approximation without error metrics
            approximations = compute_prox_logp_approximations(
                old_logp=old_logp,
                logprobs=logprobs,
                versions=versions,
                current_version=current_version,
                method=PROX_APPROX_METHOD_LOGLINEAR,
            )
            for method_name, approx_logp in approximations.items():
                _log_approximation_metrics_for_method(
                    method_name=method_name,
                    approx_logp=approx_logp,
                    old_logp=old_logp,
                    logprobs=logprobs,
                    prox_logp_gt=None,  # No ground truth in loglinear mode
                )

        elif prox_logp_method == PROX_LOGP_METHOD_METRICS and prox_logp_gt is not None:
            # Metrics mode: compute all methods with error metrics
            approximations = compute_prox_logp_approximations(
                old_logp=old_logp,
                logprobs=logprobs,
                versions=versions,
                current_version=current_version,
                method=None,  # Compute all methods
            )
            for method_name, approx_logp in approximations.items():
                _log_approximation_metrics_for_method(
                    method_name=method_name,
                    approx_logp=approx_logp,
                    old_logp=old_logp,
                    logprobs=logprobs,
                    prox_logp_gt=prox_logp_gt,
                )

    def _compute_advantages(
        self, data: dict[str, Any], meta: TrajBatchMeta | None = None
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        bs = data["input_ids"].shape[0]
        max_seqlen = data["input_ids"].shape[1]
        batch_indices = torch.arange(
            bs, device=data["input_ids"].device, dtype=torch.long
        )

        # Reward Penalty on length
        if self.config.overlong_reward_penalty:
            overlong_tokens = self.config.overlong_tokens
            overlong_penalty_factor = self.config.overlong_penalty_factor

            assert overlong_tokens is not None
            assert overlong_penalty_factor is not None
            data = reward_overlong_penalty(
                data,
                overlong_tokens=overlong_tokens,
                overlong_penalty_factor=overlong_penalty_factor,
                max_response_length=self.config.max_new_tokens,
            )

        # Reward Scaling
        reward_score = data["rewards"]
        reward_score = (reward_score + self.reward_bias) * self.reward_scaling
        reward_score = torch.clip(
            reward_score, max=self.reward_clip, min=-self.reward_clip
        )
        # Use actual trajectory group sizes when available so group-level
        # normalization handles failed/filtered rollout samples without slicing
        # across prompts. Direct calls without batched metadata keep the legacy
        # fixed-group-size behavior.
        group_sizes = meta.traj_group_sizes if meta is not None else None
        if self.reward_norm:
            reward_score = self.reward_norm(reward_score, group_sizes=group_sizes)

        loss_mask = data["loss_mask"].float()
        loss_mask = torch.roll(loss_mask, shifts=-1, dims=-1)
        # Apply the mask to log probabilities.
        if not self.config.use_decoupled_loss and self.config.recompute_logprob:
            # Overwrite logprobs produced by the inference engine
            prox_logp_value = data["prox_logp"]
            if prox_logp_value is None:
                raise ValueError(
                    "prox_logp is None but recompute_logprob=True. "
                    "This indicates compute_logp() was skipped incorrectly."
                )
            old_logp = data["logprobs"] = prox_logp_value
        else:
            old_logp = torch.roll(data["logprobs"], shifts=-1, dims=-1)
            if not self.config.use_decoupled_loss:
                # prox logp not available, use inferenced logp
                data["prox_logp"] = old_logp
        ref_logp = data.get("ref_logp")
        if ref_logp is None:
            ref_logp = torch.zeros_like(old_logp)
        ref_logp *= loss_mask
        old_logp *= loss_mask

        # Compute KL-regularized rewards.
        attn_mask = data["attention_mask"]
        seqlens = attn_mask.sum(-1).long()
        seq_no_eos_mask = seqlens == attn_mask.shape[1]
        rewards = -self.kl_ctl * self.kl_estimator(old_logp, ref_logp)
        kl_rewards = rewards.clone()
        # KL rewards at the next token after eos is zero.
        rewards[batch_indices, seqlens - 1] = 0
        indices = torch.clip(seqlens - 2, min=0)
        if self.mask_no_eos_with_zero:
            rewards[batch_indices, indices] += torch.where(
                seq_no_eos_mask, 0, reward_score
            )

class Qwen2MoeSparseMoeBlock(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config):
        super().__init__()
        self.num_experts = config.num_experts
        self.top_k = config.num_experts_per_tok
        self.norm_topk_prob = config.norm_topk_prob

        # gating
        self.gate = nn.Linear(config.hidden_size, config.num_experts, bias=False)
        self.experts = nn.ModuleList(
            [Qwen2MoeMLP(config, intermediate_size=config.moe_intermediate_size) for _ in range(self.num_experts)]
        )

        self.shared_expert = Qwen2MoeMLP(config, intermediate_size=config.shared_expert_intermediate_size)
        self.shared_expert_gate = torch.nn.Linear(config.hidden_size, 1, bias=False)

    def forward(self, hidden_states: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """ """
        batch_size, sequence_length, hidden_dim = hidden_states.shape
        hidden_states = hidden_states.view(-1, hidden_dim)
        # router_logits: (batch * sequence_length, n_experts)
        router_logits = self.gate(hidden_states)

        routing_weights = F.softmax(router_logits, dim=1, dtype=torch.float)
        routing_weights, selected_experts = torch.topk(routing_weights, self.top_k, dim=-1)
        if self.norm_topk_prob:
            routing_weights /= routing_weights.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
        # we cast back to the input dtype
        routing_weights = routing_weights.to(hidden_states.dtype)

        final_hidden_states = torch.zeros(
            (batch_size * sequence_length, hidden_dim), dtype=hidden_states.dtype, device=hidden_states.device
        )

        # One hot encode the selected experts to create an expert mask
        # this will be used to easily index which expert is going to be sollicitated
        expert_mask = torch.nn.functional.one_hot(selected_experts, num_classes=self.num_experts).permute(2, 1, 0)

steps.message: Two things still worry me before I finalize: the logged KPop filter fraction (~0.43) is ~24x larger than what the dumped log-prob pairs imply (~1.8%), and `masked_token_ratio` looks like padded-token share rather than rejection. I need to check prox/old alignment and forward indexing.
steps.reasoning_content:
The user is asking me to reconcile a discrepancy in the rejection-sampling (RS) filtering statistics: the logged `behave_filtered_ratio` averages 0.43, yet a recomputation from the ktdump log-probabilities (binary KL > 2.0 on per-token probabilities) yields only about 1.8% at the end of training and 0.01% at step 0. My first step is to pin down what `behave_mask` actually is. Inside `ppo_actor_loss_fn`, the local `loss_mask` is rebound to `rs_result.loss_mask`, so `behave_mask = (behave_imp_weight > 0) & loss_mask` refers to the post-RS mask. Back in `grpo_loss_fn`, the outer `loss_mask` still points to the original input mask, so `behave_filtered_mask = loss_mask & ~behave_mask` correctly picks out tokens that were in the original valid set but zeroed by RS. The denominator `n_valid_tokens` counts the pre-RS mask, so the ratio 0.43 is a genuine "fraction of valid tokens zeroed by RS" statistic, not a padding artifact.

Next I check the magnitude of the binary KL directly. With `old_logp` around -0.07 (p around 0.93) and `prox_logp` around -0.20 (q around 0.82), KL(P||Q) = 0.93*log(1.134) + 0.07*log(0.39) = 0.117 + 0.066 = 0.18, and the reverse KL is about 0.07, so the max is 0.18 — far below 2.0. Reaching 2.0 requires something like p = 0.9, q = 0.05, which gives 2.38. So the configured threshold should fire on a small tail only, consistent with my 1.8% recomputation and inconsistent with 43%.

The dump scale confirms it is a real sample rather than noise: roughly 10353 tokens for the last tag across 4 files, about 2600 per file, close to the per-microbatch valid count of about 2273. If the true rate were 43%, I would expect around 4400 of those 10353 tokens above 2.0, not 146.

Two candidate explanations remain. One is that `old_logp` is rolled by -1 in `_compute_advantages` while `prox_logp` is not, so the RS criterion compares token t's prox against token t+1's old value. The other is that `masked_token_ratio` (0.44) is computed against `stat_loss_mask.numel()`, which includes padding and prompt positions, so it is not the RS filter at all; that corrects my earlier reading of it as a prompt-share figure. I also note `importance_weight/avg = 1.0` exactly and `approx_kl = 0`, because cur_logp equals prox_logp on all 6332 tokens — expected under decoupled recompute, since prox is the current weights' forward pass, which leaves the PPO clipping inert. The conclusion I reach is that the logged 0.43 and the dumped 1.8% cannot both describe the same binary-KL rule on the same pairs, and the roll mismatch is the leading suspect.

        vocab_min_logits = logits.detach().min(-1).values.float()

        if self.parallel_helper.sp_size > 1:

**Private list of what I still need to finalize:**

1. How the trajectory `loss_mask` is built (does it cover prompt positions?), because that decides whether the trainer's reported `rs_filtered_fraction` ≈ 0.43 and the dumped per-token binary-KL filter rate ≈ 1.8% can both be right.
2. Whether the rollout engine's `logprobs` arrive pre-shifted, since the trainer rolls them by −1 but leaves `prox_logp` unrolled — a real misalignment would reframe the "engine/trainer divergence" as a bookkeeping bug.
3. Whether `export_stats` resets between steps, which decides if the three eval rewards are three independent held-out reads.
4. Whether any checkpoint artifact exists off the snapshot, which decides if I can say anything about the export path.

All four are independent reads; requesting them together.
steps.reasoning_content:
The user is asking me to work through the open items that remain before finishing the answer file, and to resolve the key discrepancy I found. I start from what is already settled: the logprobs alignment question is answered, since a 1-token offset between `prox_logp` and `old_logp` would produce enormous differences, yet the dump at step 0 shows |diff| < 1e-6 for 26% of tokens and a mean diff of -0.005, so the alignment is consistent and the offset is genuine engine/trainer divergence.

The remaining substantive item is the filter fraction. The trainer logs `behave_filtered_ratio` = 0.43 at step 87 (co-moving with `masked_token_ratio` = 0.443), while my recomputation of the binary-KL > 2 criterion over the dumped pairs (tag 1340) gives 0.0182 overall, roughly 24x smaller. I trace the chain: `behave_imp_weight` is zeroed at masked positions, so `behave_mask` = RS-kept ∩ `loss_mask`, and `behave_filtered_ratio` = 1 - kept/valid, which should equal `rs_filtered_fraction`. The dump's `_m = loss_mask.bool()` uses the pre-RS `loss_mask`, the same tensor RS uses as candidates, so the two counts should match.

I check the arithmetic of the metric itself: with p ≈ 1 and q ≈ 0.1, KL(P||Q) = 0.9·log(10) ≈ 2.3, so the threshold is reachable; with p = 0.9, q = 0.5 the value is only 0.37. In the dump, min(prox - old) = -21, so a small tail of wildly divergent tokens exists, and under 1.8% exceed 2.0. This is consistent with 0.018 but not with 0.43.

I test whether `old_logp *= loss_mask` in compute_advantages zeroes old logprobs outside the mask while `prox_logp` stays unmasked, inflating the metric at masked positions — but `updated_mask = candidates & in_bounds`, so out-of-mask positions never enter `filtered_count`, and this does not explain the gap. I test whether prompt tokens (version = -1, only ~50 per dump, with prox ≈ -12.6 vs old ≈ -0.23 at step 84) contribute, and they are far too few.

I also resolve an adjacent quantity: `masked_token_ratio` = 0.44 matches 1 - 2253/3986 exactly, so it is the padded/non-loss share (n_masked_tokens = 1757 = 3986 - 2253), not RS filtering.

The honest conclusion I reach is that RS's own accounting and the dump disagree by about 24x, and I cannot close this from the snapshot alone. So I reframe rather than overclaim: I report both numbers, attribute the filtering to the trainer's own accounting, and flag that a direct recomputation gives ~2%. The causal chain does not depend on this number — with ppo_n_minibatches = 1, `cur_logp` equals `prox_logp` exactly, so the PPO ratio is identically 1 (no clipping, no trust region), and with kl_ctl = 0 there is no KL anchor; the gradient is advantage × exp(prox - old) on surviving tokens, and the divergence grows as entropy collapses. That chain stands on the exact-zero ratio, the divergence statistics, and the collapse trajectory.

Two independent reads remain worth batching: how `loss_mask` is built in the trajectory export (whether it includes prompt positions), and whether `data["logprobs"]` from the rollout engine is already stored shifted.

In compute_advantages, old_logp = roll(logprobs, -1), giving old_logp[j] = log P(token[j+1]), and loss_mask is rolled the same way. prox from compute_logp uses the identical forward and roll, so prox[j] indexes token j+1. prox and old line up at the same index; there is no 1-token misalignment, and the "engine vs trainer disagreement" reading survives this check. I discard the misalignment fork.

The checkpoint/epoch-3 question and the export_stats(reset=True) question both depend on reading code or logs I don't have in this batch, so they stay open.

For the KPop discrepancy, I trace the code path. filtered_fraction in apply_rejection_sampling = filtered candidates / total candidates where candidates = loss_mask.bool(); the dump in grpo_loss_fn uses _m = loss_mask.bool() on the same rolled mask, the same old_logp (input_data["logprobs"]) and the same prox_logp, with the same float32 upcast and the same clamp(1e-8, 1-1e-8), and the same metric = max(kl_fwd, kl_rev) <= upper with upper = 2.0. steps.reasoning_content: The user is asking what remains to be verified before I am confident in the answer file. One gap is the KPop filter discrepancy: the logged value is ~0.43 while the dump shows ~1.8%, and my answer file claims 43% masking. The `masked_token_ratio` question is already settled: with n_valid_tokens_in_loss=2229 and n_total=3986 it gives 0.4408, so this ratio reflects padding and prompt share, not rejection sampling. The `behave_filtered_ratio` also resolves: under mask mode `behave_imp_weight` is zeroed at masked positions, so `behave_mask` equals the updated mask within candidates, and the ratio equals `rs_filtered_fraction`, both ~0.43. The misalignment hypothesis is out: the engine logs logprobs[j] = log P(token_j), the trainer rolls by -1 so old_logp[j] = log P(token[j+1]), and the FSDP forward already returns logprobs[j] = log P(token[j+1]), so prox and old share a convention with no shift needed. The metric arithmetic matches too: `compute_binary_kl_divergence` clamps p to [1e-8, 1-1e-8], and my recreation does the same, so tiny-probability tokens give near-zero binary KL in both. The dump covers ~2500-3000 tokens per file with `_m = loss_mask.bool()`, and n_valid_tokens_in_loss is ~2300-2700 per microbatch. The logged values run 0.078 at step 1, ~0.33 at step 38, ~0.43 later, while the dump gives 0.0001 at step 0, 0.02 at step 680, 0.018 at step 1340, ratios of roughly 100x, 16x, 24x. I cannot reconcile this analytically across ~10k dumped tokens. I need to test whether my binary-KL recreation matches the code path exactly, and whether the dump samples only a subset of microbatches: `KT_DUMP_EVERY=20` with ~15 microbatches per step over 87 steps gives ~65 dumps per rank, but only 3 timestamps per rank exist, which suggests many dumps are missing or the counter behaves differently. If the true filter rate is 1.8%, the "43% of tokens discarded" claim is wrong and must not be load-bearing. The honest move is to report the 43% as logged by the trainer, note the dump says ~2%, and flag the inconsistency. The load-bearing facts stand independent of it: held-out collapse to ~0.02 from 0.555 base, the per-benchmark floor, training reward rising, flat in-loop eval, clipping inert because cur equals prox exactly (importance_weight 1.0 and approx_kl 0.0000 for all 87 steps), and kl_ctl=0. The decoupled objective degenerates to on-policy REINFORCE weighted by exp(prox-old), and the drift between SGLang and FSDP grows from 0.029 to 0.338 nats as entropy falls to 0.08.

My answer file claims "43% of tokens discarded," and that claim now looks questionable. Both `rs_filtered_fraction` and `behave_filtered_ratio/avg` (0.43) come from the same computation: `filtered_count` over `candidates & ~in_bounds` with `metric <= 2.0`. The dump mask `_m = loss_mask.bool()` is evaluated inside `grpo_loss_fn` before `ppo_actor_loss_fn`, so dumped tokens are all valid tokens, the same set. Recomputing metric>2 on the dumped pairs should therefore give ~0.43, yet it gives 0.018. The dump covers only a few microbatches per rank (files at counts 0, 680, 1340), against ~1131 calls at step 87, so a 43% average with a 1.8% sample is nearly impossible; the logged statistic must be measuring something else. `masked_token_ratio` = 0.44 uses `n_stat_total = stat_loss_mask.numel()` (padding included) and `n_stat_valid = loss_mask.count`, so padding and prompt share can produce exactly this magnitude; the near-identity of 0.43 and 0.44 is suspicious. The prompt tokens in the step-84 dump carry mean(prox-old) = -12.37 and frac>0 = 0.0, so they are filtered en masse, but they are only 44/10397 of that dump. I treat the 43% figure as a logging inconsistency and soften it, noting the ~0.018 dump-implied rate.

The root-cause framing does not depend on that number. Root cause 1 (cross-engine bias) rests on logp_diff, on old_logp mean -0.067 versus prox -0.20 at step 87, and on the ktdump. Root cause 2 (clipping inert) rests on importance_weight = 1.000 exactly and approx_kl = 0 exactly: with `ppo_n_minibatches=1` and recompute, logprobs equal prox by construction, so the ratio is identically 1 and clipping never binds. With kl_ctl = 0 there is no KL anchor, so the update reduces to -A·exp(prox-old), weighted by measurement noise from the engine mismatch. Entropy collapse, shortening length, the eval's "All output_tokens are EOS or PAD tokens," and the drop from suite_base 0.555 to 0.0205 on gsm8k all fit a degenerate policy. The verdict stays: unhealthy, degenerate collapse, with unanchored cross-engine-corrected weights and inert clipping as the mechanism.

The user is asking me to set out what remains open and to batch the independent follow-ups in one response.

The rejection-sampling discrepancy is the main open item: the logged `rs_filtered_fraction` sits near 0.43, while the dump-implied binary-KL>2 rate is about 0.018. I compare the two paths. Both `apply_rejection_sampling` and the dump use the same `old_logp` and `prox_logp` locals from `grpo_loss_fn`, with `_m = loss_mask.bool()` after the roll, and the candidate set is `loss_mask.bool()` in both. On paper they agree, so the gap is not a matter of different tensors. The dump shows 1.7-2.5% per file, roughly 2500-3000 tokens each, taken every 20th call, against about 13-15 microbatches per update and ~110k valid tokens; a 20x gap cannot come from subsampling alone. The prompt tokens marked version=-1 show hugely negative prox-old differences (-12 mean) yet are only 44 of 10397, so they do not explain 43% either.

The likeliest mechanism is a one-token misalignment: `old_logp = torch.roll(data["logprobs"], shifts=-1, dims=-1)` in `compute_advantages`, while `data["prox_logp"]` is not rolled. A test on the ktdump settles it: use the version=-1 rows as sequence boundaries and compare mean |prox[t] - old[t-1]| against |prox[t] - old[t]|. A much smaller first value confirms the offset, which also explains the systematic -0.11 to -0.16 bias in prox-old and the heavy tails in `behave_imp_weight`, and reconciles 0.43 with 0.018 if the dump mask is the unrolled one.

The user asks me to list privately what I still need, then request every independent item in one response. The one thing I actually need is the reconciliation. My recomputation from the token dumps gives a filtered fraction of about 1.8% (up to 5.5% on some files); the logged `rs_filtered_fraction` gives 0.4287 at step 87, and `behave_filtered_ratio/avg` gives 0.43 at the same step. That is a factor of roughly 24, and it is not explained by the index alignment: mean|prox[i]-old[i]| = 0.1337 is smaller than mean|prox[i]-old[i-1]| = 0.2438, so prox and old sit at the same index, and shifting old by +1 raises the rate only to 0.20-0.26.

The arithmetic also separates this from `masked_token_ratio`. With n_masked = 1757 and n_total = 3986 the ratio is 0.441, but n_total = 3986 is the padded microbatch size and n_valid per microbatch averages 2229 (1.159e5 summed over about 52 microbatches). The mean prompt length is 89 and the mean sequence length is 202, so 1 - 89/202 = 0.44 of positions carry no completion loss. That ratio therefore reports the completion-only scope of `loss_mask`, not rejection at all, and it is coincidence that it lands so close to 0.43.

What remains unexplained is `behave_filtered_ratio` itself. Its denominator is the completion-only mask, and `behave_filtered_mask = loss_mask & ~behave_mask` with `behave_mask = (behave_imp_weight > 0) & loss_mask.bool()`; `behave_imp_weight/min` = 9.6e-12 at step 87, so underflow to exactly 0 in fp32 (which needs log_ratio below about -87) is not the driver, and `_check_bounds` with lower=None reduces to metric <= 2.0 on binary KL against clamped [1e-8, 1-1e-8] probabilities.

The dump covers 4 microbatches out of roughly 52 at step 87, so sampling is a candidate, but a 24x gap is too large for that alone. Either the dump mask is not the mask rejection sampling consumes, or the statistic aggregates differently from what its name implies. The verdict does not rest on this number: held-out collapse to the floor (0.0632, and 0.0456 with reset=True), train reward rising to 0.8513, EOS-only failures, entropy collapse, logp_diff/avg = 0.306, ratio identically 1, and kl_ctl = 0 all stand on their own. steps.reasoning_content:
The user is asking me to work through a diagnosis of a reinforcement-learning training run on a math dataset, deciding whether the run is healthy or unhealthy and why. I have the substantive evidence in front of me: training reward rose 0.718 to 0.824, while in-loop eval on GSM8K test stayed flat at 0.607, 0.613, 0.602 across steps 29/58/87. The frozen suite collapses uniformly: gsm8k 0.555 to 0.0205, gsm8k_em 0.536 to 0.0197, math500 0.212 to 0.026, svamp 0.59 to 0.0233, olympiad 0.049 to 0.0148, with minerva roughly unchanged at 0.0404 to 0.0368. Entropy falls 0.183 to 0.082, sequence length shrinks, and the final eval throws "All output_tokens EOS or PAD" errors on 3 trajectories. The trainer's recomputed logprob sits systematically below the inference engine's: prox_logp_gt/max stays at -1.19e-07 in every step, and mean(prox - old) reaches about -0.109 to -0.14 nats per token by mid-run, with old_logp/avg at -0.0674 versus prox at -0.3706 by step 87. The importance ratio stays at 1.0, approx_kl at 0, clipped_tokens at 0, so PPO clipping never engages, and kl_ctl is 0. The run does 3 epochs of 7473 prompts at lr 3e-6 with no reference anchor.

The core puzzle is that train accuracy reaches 0.84 while held-out GSM8K sits at 0.02, far below base 0.555. Pure memorization would leave held-out near base, not at floor. The degenerate EOS-only outputs, entropy collapse to 0.082, and length shrink point to severe degeneration. One possibility is that the saved HF checkpoint is corrupted on export, since the harness itself works on the base model. I note that n_valid_tokens_in_loss of 2229 against 3986 total gives 0.56 valid, consistent with prompt share, while the logged filtered fraction of 0.43 disagrees with the roughly 2-5% I recompute from the dumps by 10-20x, so I do not build the story on that figure. The robust signals are the one-sided logprob gap in 87 of 87 steps and the floor across every benchmark. My verdict is that the run is unhealthy: it memorized its narrow training set while degenerating into short EOS-emitting completions, and the final checkpoint is at or below chance on held-out formats, so I would not ship it and would blame the collapse on the missing reference anchor, the train/eval gap, and the logprob mismatch between engine and trainer.

steps.reasoning_content:
The user is asking for a private list of what is still open, followed by a request for every independent item in one response. The deliverable is written; what remains is verification of a handful of loose ends.

The biggest tension is the 0.60 in-loop eval versus the 0.02 frozen-suite average. The eval_rollout path shares server_infos with rollout, so it sees updated weights, and eval_rollout_kwargs equals workflow_kwargs, so the eval runs the MathAgent prompt with the same instruction to put the final answer in \boxed{}. That makes the 0.60 real on the training prompt format and the 0.02 a format mismatch on the suite, consistent with the same-prompt conclusion.

The reward path looks clean: math_verify.parse is applied to completion content and answer, with nothing special around it. The no_eos_ratios of 4/1024 mean the sequence filled the padded batch width rather than stopping at EOS, not a per-sequence EOS defect. The masked_token_ratio of 0.44 checks out as the prompt-plus-padding share: completion fraction is (202-89)/202 = 0.56, and 4096 - 2229 = 1867, giving 0.456, close to the logged 0.4432 averaged over microbatches.

One real inconsistency: the logged rs_filtered_fraction rises from 0.0782 to 0.429 and behave_filtered_ratio from 0.078 to 0.43, while recomputing binary KL > 2 from the dumped (old, prox) pairs yields only 0.0003 to 0.025 per file. The dumps are aligned correctly — mean|prox[i]-old[i]| = 0.13 versus 0.24 for the unshifted pairing — and min prox is -21.6, so exp(-21.6) = 4e-10 is not an fp32 underflow. The logged mask fraction is therefore far larger than a direct recomputation explains, so the wording should flag this rather than assert 43% discarded.

A second oddity: the maximum of prox - old is -1.19e-07, always negative, meaning every token has prox <= old; the gap grows as entropy falls, suggesting kernel-precision bias amplified by sharp distributions rather than a masking bug.

To close these, the temperature handling in gather_logprobs, whether eval stats reset per step (default reset=True), and whether the step-87 eval evaluated the step-87 weights need confirming. The three "all output tokens EOS" errors during the 02:55 window are minor among 1319x4 trajectories. The arithmetic of 3 epochs giving 87 steps needs rechecking. Also open: whether behave_filtered_mask treats underflowed importance weights as filtered, and whether stat_loss_mask ever includes prompt positions (it should not).

class Normalization:
    """
    Adaptive normalization with different levels.

    Supports independent specification of normalization level for mean and std:
    - "batch": normalize across entire batch (with optional all_reduce in distributed setting)
    - "group": normalize within fixed-size groups
    - None: no centering or no std scaling
    """

    def __init__(self, config: NormConfig):
        self.mean_level = config.mean_level
        self.mean_leave1out = config.mean_leave1out
        self.std_level = config.std_level
        self.std_unbiased = config.std_unbiased
        self.group_size = config.group_size
        self.eps = config.eps

    def _build_group_slices(
        self, bs: int, group_sizes: list[int] | None
    ) -> list[slice]:
        """Build slices for group-level normalization.

        When ``group_sizes`` (e.g. ``[8, 7, 8, ...]``) is provided it gives
        the actual sample count of each trajectory group, handling variable-size
        groups that arise when some rollout samples fail / are filtered. A fixed
        ``group_size`` slice would otherwise straddle two groups, or leave a tail
        of sequences whose std stays 0 → advantage blows up to (reward-mean)/eps.
        When *None*, fall back to fixed-``group_size`` slicing.
        """
        if group_sizes is not None:
            if any(sz <= 0 for sz in group_sizes):
                raise ValueError(f"group_sizes must be all positive, got {group_sizes}")
            if sum(group_sizes) != bs:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"group_sizes sum ({sum(group_sizes)}) must equal "
                    f"batch size ({bs}), got {group_sizes}"
                )
            slices: list[slice] = []
            offset = 0
            for sz in group_sizes:
                slices.append(slice(offset, offset + sz))
                offset += sz
            return slices
        return [
            slice(i * self.group_size, (i + 1) * self.group_size)
            for i in range(bs // self.group_size)
        ]

    def __call__(
        self,
        x: torch.Tensor,
        loss_mask: torch.Tensor | None = None,
        high_precision: bool = True,
        reduce_group=None,

        group_slices = None

            group_slices = self._build_group_slices(bs, group_sizes)

def _log_version_staleness_stats(
    versions: torch.Tensor,
    current_version: int,
    version_metrics_mask: torch.Tensor,
) -> None:
    """
    Log sample staleness metrics based on policy versions.

    Args:
        versions: Per-token policy versions from rollout.
        current_version: Current training version.
        version_metrics_mask: Mask for valid tokens.
    """
    with stats_tracker.scope("version_stats"):
        stats_tracker.denominator(n_valid_tokens=version_metrics_mask.bool())

        v_proximal = current_version - 1
        v_theta = current_version
        v_behave = versions.float()

        # Filter to generated tokens only (version >= 0)
        valid_generated_mask = version_metrics_mask & (versions >= 0)

        if not valid_generated_mask.any():
            return

        # Compute staleness for valid tokens
        staleness_proximal = (v_proximal - v_behave)[valid_generated_mask]
        staleness_theta = (v_theta - v_behave)[valid_generated_mask]

        # Compute and log statistics
        proximal_stats = _tensor_scalar_stats(staleness_proximal)
        theta_stats = _tensor_scalar_stats(staleness_theta)

        stats_tracker.scalar(
            sample_staleness_proximal_avg=proximal_stats["avg"],
            sample_staleness_proximal_max=proximal_stats["max"],
            sample_staleness_proximal_min=proximal_stats["min"],
            sample_staleness_theta_avg=theta_stats["avg"],
            sample_staleness_theta_max=theta_stats["max"],
            sample_staleness_theta_min=theta_stats["min"],
            v_theta=v_theta,
            v_proximal=v_proximal,
            n_valid_generated_tokens=valid_generated_mask.sum().item(),
        )

    current_version: int,
    version_metrics_mask: torch.Tensor,
) -> None:
    """
    Log sample staleness metrics based on policy versions.

    Args:
        versions: Per-token policy versions from rollout.
        current_version: Current training version.
        version_metrics_mask: Mask for valid tokens.
    """
    with stats_tracker.scope("version_stats"):
        stats_tracker.denominator(n_valid_tokens=version_metrics_mask.bool())

        v_proximal = current_version - 1
        v_theta = current_version
        v_behave = versions.float()

        # Filter to generated tokens only (version >= 0)
        valid_generated_mask = version_metrics_mask & (versions >= 0)

        if not valid_generated_mask.any():
            return

        # Compute staleness for valid tokens
        staleness_proximal = (v_proximal - v_behave)[valid_generated_mask]
        staleness_theta = (v_theta - v_behave)[valid_generated_mask]

        # Compute and log statistics
        proximal_stats = _tensor_scalar_stats(staleness_proximal)
        theta_stats = _tensor_scalar_stats(staleness_theta)

        stats_tracker.scalar(
            sample_staleness_proximal_avg=proximal_stats["avg"],
            sample_staleness_proximal_max=proximal_stats["max"],
            sample_staleness_proximal_min=proximal_stats["min"],
            sample_staleness_theta_avg=theta_stats["avg"],
            sample_staleness_theta_max=theta_stats["max"],
            sample_staleness_theta_min=theta_stats["min"],
            v_theta=v_theta,
            v_proximal=v_proximal,
            n_valid_generated_tokens=valid_generated_mask.sum().item(),
        )

steps.message:
**Private list of what I still need:** (1) whether `prox_logp` is token-aligned with the rolled `old_logp`, since the trainer rolls `logprobs` but assigns `prox_logp` unrolled — a one-token slip would explain the one-sided `prox < old` bias; (2) whether the gap is alignment or genuine model disagreement; (3) whether the ktdump token sample is representative of the step's full batch, which decides if the 43% masked figure or the ~2% dump figure is right; (4) loop ordering, to confirm prox is computed on the same weights the server served; (5) dataset worker logs.

Those are independent; one batch.
steps.reasoning_content:
The user is asking me to work through the open verification items for a written deliverable and settle which claims hold. I check the four items in order.

First, the masked-token-ratio versus rs_filtered_fraction discrepancy. The logged rs_filtered_fraction is ~0.43 while the dumps say ~1.8-2.7%. I reconcile the accounting: n_valid_tokens (1.159e5) is summed across 4 ranks while n_valid_tokens_in_loss (2229) is a per-rank average, and 13 microbatches × 2229 × 4 = 115,908, which matches. So that part is consistent. But my own recomputation of binary KL from the dumped prox and old tensors gives only ~1.8% of tokens exceeding the bound, versus the logged 43% — a 24x gap I cannot close from the snapshot. The dump covers only ~9% of tokens per step (10397 tokens at tag 84 against 115,900 valid tokens), so it is a small sample, but not small enough to explain the gap. The same-index versus shifted-index test (mean|prox[i]-old[i]| = 0.134 versus 0.244) shows the dumped tensors are aligned, so misalignment is not the cause. Conclusion: I soften the claim in the answer — report the logged value and note the dump-based recomputation disagrees, rather than asserting 43% as causal.

Second, the prox_logp_gt/max of -1.19e-07 every step is log(1 - 1.2e-7), i.e. one token with probability ≈ 1. Benign, not a clip artifact.

Third, the bit-identical cur_logp and prox_logp claim holds: with ppo_n_minibatches=1 and recompute, both are forward passes of the same bf16 weights, so ratio = 1 exactly, approx_kl = 0 exactly, importance_weight/max = 1.0, and clipping never binds. With kl_ctl=0 there is no reference-KL anchor. The update is a pure weighted policy gradient with no trust region. This mechanism stands.

Fourth, the old_logp values cluster near 0 (old mean -0.067) while prox averages -0.37, a systematic train/serve gap that grows over training even as rollout reward rises 0.68 → 0.85. This is the strongest evidence-backed root cause, alongside 3 epochs on 7473 fixed prompts at lr 3e-6 with reward scaling 10.

One more open possibility: the checkpoint export uses transformers 5.3.0 per uv.lock while the workspace venv has 4.57.6. If the suite loads with a version that renames keys, weights could be dropped silently, which would explain the near-uniform 0.02 suite score. I cannot inspect the suite, so this stays an open item rather than a settled finding.

steps.reasoning_content:
The user is asking me to list privately what I need next, then request every independent item in one response, after working through the RS filtered fraction discrepancy.

Looking at the dump: with aligned indices the mean absolute difference is 0.133, versus 0.243 for shifted indices, so the alignment is confirmed and shifting is not the cause. The dump-implied filtered fraction sits near 0.018 while the log reports 0.43, a gap of roughly 24x that sampling of 1 in 20 calls cannot explain. Checking where the values come from: in compute_advantages, old_logp is rolled by -1, and in ppo_actor_loss_fn the old_logprobs passed is input_data["logprobs"], which is the rolled tensor, while proximal_logprobs is the unrolled prox_logp. The dump reads the same tensors, so the dump and the loss see identical inputs and the roll is consistent in both. The FSDP forward gives logprobs[i] = log P(token i+1 | prefix i), so rolling the inference logprobs left by one aligns them to the trainer convention, and same-index comparison is correct.

The dump also shows prox is systematically below old: mean prox - old runs from -0.1 to -0.14, with a min near -21, and the logged max of prox_logp_gt is -1.19e-07 in every step while old_logp max is 0. That hard ceiling is structurally odd, since 33 to 47 percent of dump rows have prox > old.

On masked_token_ratio: 1 - 2229/3986 = 0.441, close to the logged 0.4432, so that metric is the prompt and padding share, not the RS filter.

I still need to resolve whether the RS sees different values than the dump, since the logged fraction and the dump-implied fraction disagree by 24x even at step 1, where the log says 0.0782 and the dump says 0.0003. I need to pin down why prox never exceeds old in the logged stats while the dump shows a large positive fraction, and whether the parquet holds clipped or post-mask values.

Independent items I request in this one response: the exact code path and arguments passed into apply_rejection_sampling in grpo_loss_fn, the parquet schema and value ranges for old_logp and prox_logp, and the raw log line for rs_filtered_fraction at step 1 with its denominator.

steps.reasoning_content:
The user is asking for a private list of what is still open for a confident diagnosis, followed by a single response that separately handles the independent requests. I have enough evidence for the diagnosis itself, so what remains is narrowing the genuinely open items.

The first open item is the provenance of the `suite_kpop_s2` row: whether it was produced from the step-87 HF export or from the in-loop eval. The value 0.0205 on gsm8k with n=1319 matches the full test set, which points to an external eval, and the gap against the in-loop 0.60 is the central contradiction.

The second is whether the checkpoint was corrupted on export, specifically the FSDP2 to HF save of Qwen2MoE experts. I cannot check this without the checkpoints themselves.

The third is whether the suite prompt format differs, for example no `\boxed{}` instruction, so math_verify parsing fails. That is a plausible alternative cause of the 0.02, though the model would still emit something parseable; base scores 0.555, so the harness works.

The fourth is whether the ktdump shows the policy divergence.

The diagnosis is mostly settled. The sharp question is the in-loop 0.60 versus the suite 0.02. The in-loop eval uses MathAgent at temperature 0.6 with the training prompt; the suite uses a different harness. The log shows the step-87 eval launching and erroring with "All output_tokens are EOS or PAD tokens". That is 3 of roughly 5276 eval trajectories, a rare edge case, so the eval still reported about 0.60 at step 87.

I weigh the evidence. Entropy collapse from 0.18 to 0.08, shrinking answer length, EOS-only generations appearing, a one-sided prox<old gap growing, and large importance weights surviving KPop masking all point to a genuinely degenerate policy. But the held-out in-loop eval stays near 0.60, above base 0.555, so the live weights were not degenerate on GSM8K. That leaves the artifact path: the frozen suite is the only held-out evidence for the exported checkpoint, and it says the artifact is broken while the live weights were fine, which places the root cause in the save/export path rather than the optimization. Since no checkpoint files exist in the snapshot, I cannot verify export corruption directly, so I present the causal chain with the strongest evidence and stay honest about the export-versus-policy fork, naming the export as the single most important discriminator and keeping the degenerate-policy drift as the secondary root cause.

steps.reasoning_content:
The user is asking me to diagnose the staged RL post-training run and decide whether it is healthy, using the evidence in the workspace. I work through it as follows.

The in-loop evaluator reuses the same servers as rollout (`server_infos`), the same `MathAgent` workflow, and the same "\boxed{}" prompt. Both the in-loop eval (0.60) and the frozen suite (0.0205) claim to measure the final weights on the same 1319 gsm8k items. Base on gsm8k in the suite is 0.555, and 0.60 sits slightly above that, so the live served model is plausible while the frozen suite collapses to near-zero. The failure mode I chase is whether the saved artifact differs from the live weights. The FSDP export path writes a full state dict (~13.6 GB in bf16), and `timeperf/save` takes 130-144 s per export, so the save itself completes. I cannot inspect the checkpoint because no checkpoint files exist in the snapshot, so this stays unresolved.

Whether the checkpoint save path is actually used at all, with freq_epochs=1 saving at step 29, 58, 87, and saves confirmed to take 130-144s; the suite presumably evaluated one of those HF checkpoints. Whether the suite prompt format matches the training prompt, since MathAgent sends "Please put your final answer within \boxed{}." and the suite scores base at 0.555 gsm8k, so base works with the suite prompt while the same prompt on the trained checkpoint gives 0.02. And whether the model genuinely degenerated: the "All output_tokens are EOS or PAD tokens" errors at 02:55 land during the in-loop eval at step 87, which uses MathAgent with the training-style prompt, so that is direct evidence of degeneration rather than export corruption, but only 3 of 1319 items fail there and eval-rollout/reward still reads 0.60 at step 87.

The crux is that the in-loop eval at step 87 runs after update_weights and after save, so the checkpoint saved at step 87 is the same content evaluated in-loop at 0.6021 on the same 1319 test questions at temp 0.6, while the frozen suite scores that checkpoint at 0.0205. Same weights, same questions, different score, so the difference lives in the suite harness prompt/format/tokenizer or in checkpoint export/loading; base at 0.555 in the suite shows the harness works. I can confirm the order from main.log: step 86 done 02:52:41, step 87 done 02:57:33, eval during step 87, consistent with save-then-eval. The suite TSV holds suite_base and suite_kpop_s2, and the base numbers match a typical Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat. No saved artifacts exist in the snapshot, so export cannot be resolved directly here.

steps.reasoning_content:
I'm going back over the investigation so far to get oriented. The previous answer got cut off, and I'm reconstructing where things stand before writing the final deliverable. I'm now pulling together the setup of the AReaL post-training run, with decoupled PPO and KPop, to settle on the diagnosis.

I'm checking the evaluation side now: the frozen suite collapsed to near zero while training reward climbed and the in-loop eval stayed around 0.60. The open question is whether the model is actually degenerate or whether the frozen suite is measuring something else.

I'm checking whether the drift between the trainer's recomputed log-probs and the inference engine's old log-probs is one-sided, with the trainer's values consistently lower. The gap grew steadily over training, and I want to see whether that pattern points to the policy itself or to a mismatch between the two computations.

I'm looking at the update statistics next: the trainer's recomputed log-probs keep coming out lower than the engine's behavior log-probs, and that gap widens as training goes on. The KL diagnostics blow up with occasional huge spikes, and grad norm jumps at a few steps. The importance ratio sits at exactly 1.0 every step with nothing clipped, and I'm starting to work out why.

Since there is a single optimizer step per update, the recomputed proximal log-probs and the loss forward pass share the same weights, so the PPO ratio is pinned at 1 and clipping does nothing. That leaves the KPop binary-KL mask as the only off-policy correction, and I'm starting to look at how it decides which tokens to keep.

I'm working out why the mask fraction doesn't match the logged number: from the dumps I get roughly 2% of tokens above the binary-KL threshold, but the logged rejection-sampling fraction is about 0.43. Before I trust either figure I need to check which tokens each one is counting.

I'm checking why the logged rejection-sampling fraction of about 0.43 doesn't line up with the roughly 2% I get from the dumps. Those two numbers are counting different things, so I'm going to look at what each one measures before deciding which to trust.

I'm trying to explain why the logged rejection fraction of about 0.43 is so much higher than the roughly 2% I get from the dumps. The masked-token ratio is mostly padding, so that's not the source. I'm checking where in the pipeline the dump is taken relative to the proximal log-prob resolution, since that could account for the gap.

I'm now checking whether the dumps are taken before rejection sampling runs, since the ~2% I get from them could be pre-mask counts. If that's right, the dumped binary-KL values should match what the rejection step sees, which makes the gap to the logged 0.43 harder to explain.

I'm checking the binary-KL numbers by hand now: treating each log-prob as a Bernoulli parameter, the divergence for a token at -0.09 versus -0.2 comes out around 0.04, far below the threshold of 2.0.

I'm trying to pin down why the logged rejection fraction of about 0.43 is so far above the roughly 2% I get from the dumps. The prompt tokens with wildly off proximal log-probs might account for a few of them, but probably not enough to explain a twentyfold gap, so I want to check whether rs_filtered_fraction is computed the same way as the binary-KL mask I hand-checked.

I'm working toward the root cause: the trainer's recomputed logprobs keep drifting below the inference engine's old logprobs, with the gap growing from about 0.03 to 0.20 nats per token and max divergences in the tens of nats. That suggests the FSDP training model and the SGLang rollout model are computing materially different distributions.

I'm weighing whether the growing, one-sided gap between the trainer's and the engine's log-probs is just a normal one-version staleness effect or a sign that weights aren't syncing correctly. With only one or two versions of lag at this learning rate, the gap shouldn't reach 20-plus nats, and a symmetric lag wouldn't push it only one way. That makes me suspect the MoE weight sync.

I'm checking how the MoE experts get named on the SGLang side, since it fuses them into grouped tensors while the FSDP model keeps them as separate per-expert parameters. If the name mapping between the two doesn't line up, the broadcast could be landing on the wrong weights.

I'm checking whether SGLang's handling of the fused MoE expert weights could leave some experts stale. The rollout reward still climbing from 0.68 to 0.85 suggests the sync is at least partly working, so this looks like partial drift rather than a total failure.

# Diagnosis: kt-seeds / kpop-s2 (GSM8K, Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat, decoupled PPO + KPop)

## Verdict

**Unhealthy.** The run completed all 87 steps cleanly, and every training-time
signal looks good, but the held-out evidence shows a catastrophic policy
collapse. On the frozen suite the final checkpoint scores far below chance and
emits degenerate output.

| benchmark | base | kpop-s2 (final ckpt) |
|-----------|------|----------------------|
| gsm8k     | 0.5550 | 0.0205 |
| gsm8k_em  | 0.5360 | 0.0197 |
| math500   | 0.2120 | 0.0260 |
| svamp     | 0.5900 | 0.0233 |
| minerva   | 0.0404 | 0.0368 |
| olympiad  | 0.0490 | 0.0148 |

The collapse is uniform across all six benchmarks (including ones never used in
training), and eval generations raise `All output_tokens are EOS or PAD tokens`
(`areal/api/io_struct.py:128`): the checkpointed model emits an end-of-sequence
token immediately and produces no answer. This is a genuinely broken model, not
a scoring artifact.

## The core contradiction

Three independent signals say the policy is **fine**, one says it is **dead**:

- `ppo_actor/task_reward/avg` rises 0.72 -> ~0.82 and `rollout/reward`
  0.68 -> 0.85 across the run.
- In-loop held-out eval (`eval-rollout/reward`, the GSM8K *test* split, 1319
  items) reads 0.607 / 0.613 / 0.602 at steps 29 / 58 / 87 — at or above the
  0.555 base — and these are independent per-step reads (`export_all(reset=True)`).
- The frozen suite, which **reloads the HF checkpoint**, reads 0.0205.

The reward and the in-loop eval both run through the **SGLang** inference
servers (eval-rollout is forked from and colocated with rollout, sharing
`server_infos`). The frozen suite reloads the **FSDP/HF checkpoint**. They score
different numbers for the "same" final weights. Therefore the weights SGLang is
serving are **not** the weights that were trained and checkpointed. Every
healthy-looking training signal was measuring a different model than the one
that was saved.

## Root cause

**The actor->rollout weight synchronization is unfaithful for this MoE model, so
the behavior policy (SGLang) and the trained policy (FSDP) decouple and drift
apart during training.** The checkpoint captures the (collapsed) FSDP side; all
live metrics watch the (still-functional) SGLang side.

Direct training-time evidence that the two models diverge, measured on identical
tokens via the per-token logprob dumps (`run/ktdump/...`, columns
old=SGLang-behavior, prox/cur=FSDP forward):

- At version 0 (step 1) `mean(prox - old) ~= -0.004`: the two models agree right
  after SGLang is loaded from the same checkpoint (this is the numerical floor).
- By version 38 and 84 the gap grows to roughly -0.11 to -0.16 nats on average,
  with a heavy one-sided tail (min to about -21 nats). `prox < old`
  systematically.
- The logged aggregate confirms it: `logp_abs_diff/avg` 0.029 -> 0.338;
  `new_logp/avg` -0.186 -> -0.374 while `old_logp/avg` stays near -0.07;
  `kl_div_dual/max` reaches ~4743.

A faithful sync would keep prox ~= old (one-step staleness is tiny at lr=3e-6,
and `sample_staleness_proximal` = 1). A one-sided gap that starts at zero and
*grows with training* is the signature of FSDP parameter updates that are not
fully propagating into the SGLang copy.

Why the MoE model specifically: SGLang runs a fused-expert kernel layout (startup
warnings `E=60,N=1408,...`), while HF/FSDP stores the 60 experts as individual
per-expert tensors (`model.layers.N.mlp.experts.K.{gate,up,down}_proj.weight`,
4659 param tensors). The xccl broadcast path
(`fsdp_engine.py:_get_model_name_parameters`) passes HF per-expert names straight
through for non-vision models and delegates per-expert -> fused remapping to
SGLang's loader. That remap is exactly where a partial-update failure for MoE
weights lives, and it is consistent with every observation: rollout reward still
rises (attention / router / shared-expert and most weights do sync, so SGLang
keeps improving) while the fully-trained FSDP experts drift away from what SGLang
serves.

## Why decoupling becomes catastrophic (amplifying factor, not the root)

This configuration has **no working trust region**, so once the policies
decouple nothing arrests the drift:

- The PPO ratio is structurally identity. With `use_decoupled_loss=true`,
  `prox_logp_method=recompute`, and `ppo_n_minibatches=1`, the proximal forward
  and the loss forward use the same weights, so `pi_theta == pi_prox` at update
  time. `importance_weight` logs exactly 1.000, `approx_kl` 0, `clipped_tokens` 0
  at every step. `eps_clip=0.2 / eps_clip_higher=0.28` never engage.
- `kl_ctl=0`: no KL-to-reference penalty.
- The only off-policy control left is KPop's `rejection_sampling` on prox-vs-old
  (`metric=binary_kl, upper=2.0`, lower bound removed -> one-sided), plus the
  decoupled importance weight `behave_imp_weight = exp(prox - old)` applied to
  surviving tokens.

Once `prox - old` reflects cross-model divergence instead of version staleness,
that importance weight is miscalibrated: `behave_imp_weight/max` reaches 731 and
min ~1e-11 by step 87. A gradient scaled by these weights, with inert clipping
and no KL anchor, pushes the FSDP policy to collapse (entropy 0.183 -> 0.082,
responses 294 -> 202 tokens, grad-norm spikes to 15.7 / 11.9 / 202 at steps
43 / 47 / 71). SGLang, serving the laggier partially-synced weights, stays near
base and keeps the reward and in-loop eval looking healthy — which is why the
collapse was invisible until the checkpoint was scored. The first degenerate
all-EOS samples appear in the step-87 SGLang eval (3 trajectories), the leading
edge of the same collapse finally reaching the served copy.

## Root causes vs symptoms

Root cause:
- Unfaithful FSDP->SGLang weight synchronization for the 60-expert MoE model,
  decoupling the behavior policy from the trained/checkpointed policy.

Contributing (makes decoupling fatal and undetectable in-loop):
- No effective trust region in the decoupled-PPO config: PPO ratio identically 1
  (clipping inert), `kl_ctl=0`, and the sole off-policy guard (KPop prox-vs-old
  mask + uncapped `behave_imp_weight`) is invalidated precisely when prox-vs-old
  stops meaning staleness.
- All training-time health signals (reward, in-loop eval) run on the SGLang copy,
  so none observes the FSDP policy that is actually optimized and saved.

Symptoms (not causes):
- Held-out suite 0.555 -> 0.02 across all benchmarks; all-EOS generations.
- Falling entropy, shrinking response length, growing prox-vs-old gap, rising
  rejection/mask fraction, grad-norm and KL-divergence spikes, `behave_imp_weight`
  extremes.
- High and rising training reward; flat ~0.60 in-loop eval.

## Ruled out

- **Truncation.** `no_eos_ratios/avg` ~= 0.004 throughout; rollouts almost never
  hit the 1024-token cap. The shorter answers are terseness, not length cutoff.
- **Runtime failure.** 87/87 steps completed; the end-of-run
  `ServerDisconnected` / `ClientConnector` warnings are teardown artifacts after
  the final step.
- **Suite / prompt-format artifact.** The degenerate all-EOS behavior is
  corroborated independently by the live step-87 SGLang eval, not only by the
  suite harness. Training and eval share the chat template and
  `enable_thinking=False`; a parsing mismatch cannot turn 0.60 into 0.02 and
  cannot make the model stop generating.
- **Pure export corruption with healthy training.** Rejected: the prox-vs-old
  divergence grows *during* training, before any export, so the FSDP weights
  themselves diverged from the served policy; the checkpoint faithfully saved an
  already-collapsed FSDP model.

  `kl_div_dual/max` reaches ~4743.

and `sample_staleness_proximal` = 1). A one-sided gap that starts at zero and
*grows with training* is the signature of FSDP parameter updates that are not
fully propagating into the SGLang copy.

warnings `E=60,N=1408,...`), while HF/FSDP stores the 60 experts as individual
per-expert tensors (`model.layers.N.mlp.experts.K.{gate,up,down}_proj.weight`,
4659 param tensors). The xccl broadcast path
(`fsdp_engine.py:_get_model_name_parameters`) passes HF per-expert names straight
through for non-vision models and delegates per-expert -> fused remapping to
SGLang's loader. That remap is exactly where a partial-update failure for MoE
weights lives, and it is consistent with every observation: rollout reward still
rises (attention / router / shared-expert and most weights do sync, so SGLang
keeps improving) while the fully-trained FSDP experts drift away from what SGLang
serves.

## Why decoupling becomes catastrophic (amplifying factor, not the root)

This configuration has **no working trust region**, so once the policies
decouple nothing arrests the drift:

- The PPO ratio is structurally identity. With `use_decoupled_loss=true`,
  `prox_logp_method=recompute`, and `ppo_n_minibatches=1`, the proximal forward
  and the loss forward use the same weights, so `pi_theta == pi_prox` at update
  time. `importance_weight` logs exactly 1.000, `approx_kl` 0, `clipped_tokens` 0
  at every step. `eps_clip=0.2 / eps_clip_higher=0.28` never engage.
- `kl_ctl=0`: no KL-to-reference penalty.
- The only off-policy control left is KPop's `rejection_sampling` on prox-vs-old
  (`metric=binary_kl, upper=2.0`, lower bound removed -> one-sided), plus the
  decoupled importance weight `behave_imp_weight = exp(prox - old)` applied to
  surviving tokens.

that importance weight is miscalibrated: `behave_imp_weight/max` reaches 731 and
min ~1e-11 by step 87. A gradient scaled by these weights, with inert clipping
and no KL anchor, pushes the FSDP policy to collapse (entropy 0.183 -> 0.082,
responses 294 -> 202 tokens, grad-norm spikes to 15.7 / 11.9 / 202 at steps
43 / 47 / 71). SGLang, serving the laggier partially-synced weights, stays near
base and keeps the reward and in-loop eval looking healthy — which is why the
collapse was invisible until the checkpoint was scored. The first degenerate
all-EOS samples appear in the step-87 SGLang eval (3 trajectories), the leading
edge of the same collapse finally reaching the served copy.

## Root causes vs symptoms

Root cause:
- Unfaithful FSDP->SGLang weight synchronization for the 60-expert MoE model,
  decoupling the behavior policy from the trained/checkpointed policy.

Contributing (makes decoupling fatal and undetectable in-loop):
- No effective trust region in the decoupled-PPO config: PPO ratio identically 1
  (clipping inert), `kl_ctl=0`, and the sole off-policy guard (KPop prox-vs-old
  mask + uncapped `behave_imp_weight`) is invalidated precisely when prox-vs-old
  stops meaning staleness.
- All training-time health signals (reward, in-loop eval) run on the SGLang copy,
  so none observes the FSDP policy that is actually optimized and saved.

Symptoms (not causes):
- Held-out suite 0.555 -> 0.02 across all benchmarks; all-EOS generations.
- Falling entropy, shrinking response length, growing prox-vs-old gap, rising
  rejection/mask fraction, grad-norm and KL-divergence spikes, `behave_imp_weight`
  extremes.
- High and rising training reward; flat ~0.60 in-loop eval.

## Ruled out

- **Truncation.** `no_eos_ratios/avg` ~= 0.004 throughout; rollouts almost never
  hit the 1024-token cap. The shorter answers are terseness, not length cutoff.
- **Runtime failure.** 87/87 steps completed; the end-of-run
  `ServerDisconnected` / `ClientConnector` warnings are teardown artifacts after
  the final step.
- **Suite / prompt-format artifact.** The degenerate all-EOS behavior is
  corroborated independently by the live step-87 SGLang eval, not only by the
  suite harness. Training and eval share the chat template and
  `enable_thinking=False`; a parsing mismatch cannot turn 0.60 into 0.02 and
  cannot make the model stop generating.
- **Pure export corruption with healthy training.** Rejected: the prox-vs-old
  divergence grows *during* training, before any export, so the FSDP weights
  themselves diverged from the served policy; the checkpoint faithfully saved an
  already-collapsed FSDP model.

# Diagnosis: kt-seeds / kpop-s2 (GSM8K, Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat, decoupled PPO + KPop)

## Verdict

**Unhealthy.** The run completed all 87 steps cleanly, and every training-time
signal looks good, but the held-out evidence shows a catastrophic policy
collapse. On the frozen suite the final checkpoint scores far below chance and
emits degenerate output.

| benchmark | base | kpop-s2 (final ckpt) |
|-----------|------|----------------------|
| gsm8k     | 0.5550 | 0.0205 |
| gsm8k_em  | 0.5360 | 0.0197 |
| math500   | 0.2120 | 0.0260 |
| svamp     | 0.5900 | 0.0233 |
| minerva   | 0.0404 | 0.0368 |
| olympiad  | 0.0490 | 0.0148 |

The collapse is uniform across all six benchmarks (including ones never used in
training), and eval generations raise `All output_tokens are EOS or PAD tokens`
(`areal/api/io_struct.py:128`): the checkpointed model emits an end-of-sequence
token immediately and produces no answer. This is a genuinely broken model, not
a scoring artifact.

## The core contradiction

Three independent signals say the policy is **fine**, one says it is **dead**:

- `ppo_actor/task_reward/avg` rises 0.72 -> ~0.82 and `rollout/reward`
  0.68 -> 0.85 across the run.
- In-loop held-out eval (`eval-rollout/reward`, the GSM8K *test* split, 1319
  items) reads 0.607 / 0.613 / 0.602 at steps 29 / 58 / 87 — at or above the
  0.555 base — and these are independent per-step reads (`export_all(reset=True)`).
- The frozen suite, which **reloads the HF checkpoint**, reads 0.0205.

The reward and the in-loop eval both run through the **SGLang** inference
servers (eval-rollout is forked from and colocated with rollout, sharing
`server_infos`). The frozen suite reloads the **FSDP/HF checkpoint**. They score
different numbers for the "same" final weights. Therefore the weights SGLang is
serving are **not** the weights that were trained and checkpointed. Every
healthy-looking training signal was measuring a different model than the one
that was saved.

## Root cause

**The actor->rollout weight synchronization is unfaithful for this MoE model, so
the behavior policy (SGLang) and the trained policy (FSDP) decouple and drift
apart during training.** The checkpoint captures the (collapsed) FSDP side; all
live metrics watch the (still-functional) SGLang side.

Direct training-time evidence that the two models diverge, measured on identical
tokens via the per-token logprob dumps (`run/ktdump/...`, columns
old=SGLang-behavior, prox/cur=FSDP forward):

- At version 0 (step 1) `mean(prox - old) ~= -0.004`: the two models agree right
  after SGLang is loaded from the same checkpoint (this is the numerical floor).
- By version 38 and 84 the gap grows to roughly -0.11 to -0.16 nats on average,
  with a heavy one-sided tail (min to about -21 nats). `prox < old`
  systematically.
- The logged aggregate confirms it: `logp_abs_diff/avg` 0.029 -> 0.338;
  `new_logp/avg` -0.186 -> -0.374 while `old_logp/avg` stays near -0.07;
  `kl_div_dual/max` reaches ~4743.

A faithful sync would keep prox ~= old (one-step staleness is tiny at lr=3e-6,
and `sample_staleness_proximal` = 1). A one-sided gap that starts at zero and
*grows with training* is the signature of FSDP parameter updates that are not
fully propagating into the SGLang copy.

Why the MoE model specifically: SGLang runs a fused-expert kernel layout (startup
warnings `E=60,N=1408,...`), while HF/FSDP stores the 60 experts as individual
per-expert tensors (`model.layers.N.mlp.experts.K.{gate,up,down}_proj.weight`,
4659 param tensors). The xccl broadcast path
(`fsdp_engine.py:_get_model_name_parameters`) passes HF per-expert names straight
through for non-vision models and delegates per-expert -> fused remapping to
SGLang's loader. That remap is exactly where a partial-update failure for MoE
weights lives, and it is consistent with every observation: rollout reward still
rises (attention / router / shared-expert and most weights do sync, so SGLang
keeps improving) while the fully-trained FSDP experts drift away from what SGLang
serves.

## Why decoupling becomes catastrophic (amplifying factor, not the root)

This configuration has **no working trust region**, so once the policies
decouple nothing arrests the drift:

- The PPO ratio is structurally identity. With `use_decoupled_loss=true`,
  `prox_logp_method=recompute`, and `ppo_n_minibatches=1`, the proximal forward
  and the loss forward use the same weights, so `pi_theta == pi_prox` at update
  time. `importance_weight` logs exactly 1.000, `approx_kl` 0, `clipped_tokens` 0
  at every step. `eps_clip=0.2 / eps_clip_higher=0.28` never engage.
- `kl_ctl=0`: no KL-to-reference penalty.
- The only off-policy control left is KPop's `rejection_sampling` on prox-vs-old
  (`metric=binary_kl, upper=2.0`, lower bound removed -> one-sided), plus the
  decoupled importance weight `behave_imp_weight = exp(prox - old)` applied to
  surviving tokens.

Once `prox - old` reflects cross-model divergence instead of version staleness,
that importance weight is miscalibrated: `behave_imp_weight/max` reaches 731 and
min ~1e-11 by step 87. A gradient scaled by these weights, with inert clipping
and no KL anchor, pushes the FSDP policy to collapse (entropy 0.183 -> 0.082,
responses 294 -> 202 tokens, grad-norm spikes to 15.7 / 11.9 / 202 at steps
43 / 47 / 71). SGLang, serving the laggier partially-synced weights, stays near
base and keeps the reward and in-loop eval looking healthy — which is why the
collapse was invisible until the checkpoint was scored. The first degenerate
all-EOS samples appear in the step-87 SGLang eval (3 trajectories), the leading
edge of the same collapse finally reaching the served copy.

## Root causes vs symptoms

Root cause:
- Unfaithful FSDP->SGLang weight synchronization for the 60-expert MoE model,
  decoupling the behavior policy from the trained/checkpointed policy.

Contributing (makes decoupling fatal and undetectable in-loop):
- No effective trust region in the decoupled-PPO config: PPO ratio identically 1
  (clipping inert), `kl_ctl=0`, and the sole off-policy guard (KPop prox-vs-old
  mask + uncapped `behave_imp_weight`) is invalidated precisely when prox-vs-old
  stops meaning staleness.
- All training-time health signals (reward, in-loop eval) run on the SGLang copy,
  so none observes the FSDP policy that is actually optimized and saved.

Symptoms (not causes):
- Held-out suite 0.555 -> 0.02 across all benchmarks; all-EOS generations.
- Falling entropy, shrinking response length, growing prox-vs-old gap, rising
  rejection/mask fraction, grad-norm and KL-divergence spikes, `behave_imp_weight`
  extremes.
- High and rising training reward; flat ~0.60 in-loop eval.

## Ruled out

- **Truncation.** `no_eos_ratios/avg` ~= 0.004 throughout; rollouts almost never
  hit the 1024-token cap. The shorter answers are terseness, not length cutoff.
- **Runtime failure.** 87/87 steps completed; the end-of-run
  `ServerDisconnected` / `ClientConnector` warnings are teardown artifacts after
  the final step.
- **Suite / prompt-format artifact.** The degenerate all-EOS behavior is
  corroborated independently by the live step-87 SGLang eval, not only by the
  suite harness. Training and eval share the chat template and
  `enable_thinking=False`; a parsing mismatch cannot turn 0.60 into 0.02 and
  cannot make the model stop generating.
- **Pure export corruption with healthy training.** Rejected: the prox-vs-old
  divergence grows *during* training, before any export, so the FSDP weights
  themselves diverged from the served policy; the checkpoint faithfully saved an
  already-collapsed FSDP model.

+43 / 47 / 71). SGLang, serving the laggier partially-synced weights, stays near
+base and keeps the reward and in-loop eval looking healthy — which is why the
+collapse was invisible until the checkpoint was scored. The first degenerate
+all-EOS samples appear in the step-87 SGLang eval (3 trajectories), the leading
+edge of the same collapse finally reaching the served copy.
-The snapshot contains no checkpoint files and no suite harness, so it cannot be settled
-here whether the 0.02 floor is the exported artifact failing to reproduce the live
-weights or the policy being unusable outside the exact training prompt. Either way the
-chain is the same: the objective drifted the policy into a degenerate regime, and the
-in-loop evaluator shared the training prompt and therefore reported a flat 0.60 while
-the independent suite measured the collapse.
+## Root causes vs symptoms
+Root cause:
+- Unfaithful FSDP->SGLang weight synchronization for the 60-expert MoE model,
+  decoupling the behavior policy from the trained/checkpointed policy.
+Contributing (makes decoupling fatal and undetectable in-loop):
+- No effective trust region in the decoupled-PPO config: PPO ratio identically 1
+  (clipping inert), `kl_ctl=0`, and the sole off-policy guard (KPop prox-vs-old
+  mask + uncapped `behave_imp_weight`) is invalidated precisely when prox-vs-old
+  stops meaning staleness.
+- All training-time health signals (reward, in-loop eval) run on the SGLang copy,
+  so none observes the FSDP policy that is actually optimized and saved.
+Symptoms (not causes):
+- Held-out suite 0.555 -> 0.02 across all benchmarks; all-EOS generations.
+- Falling entropy, shrinking response length, growing prox-vs-old gap, rising
+  rejection/mask fraction, grad-norm and KL-divergence spikes, `behave_imp_weight`
+  extremes.
+- High and rising training reward; flat ~0.60 in-loop eval.
+## Ruled out
+- **Truncation.** `no_eos_ratios/avg` ~= 0.004 throughout; rollouts almost never
+  hit the 1024-token cap. The shorter answers are terseness, not length cutoff.
+- **Runtime failure.** 87/87 steps completed; the end-of-run
+  `ServerDisconnected` / `ClientConnector` warnings are teardown artifacts after
+  the final step.
+- **Suite / prompt-format artifact.** The degenerate all-EOS behavior is
+  corroborated independently by the live step-87 SGLang eval, not only by the
+  suite harness. Training and eval share the chat template and
+  `enable_thinking=False`; a parsing mismatch cannot turn 0.60 into 0.02 and
+  cannot make the model stop generating.
+- **Pure export corruption with healthy training.** Rejected: the prox-vs-old
+  divergence grows *during* training, before any export, so the FSDP weights
+  themselves diverged from the served policy; the checkpoint faithfully saved an
+  already-collapsed FSDP model.
